description: Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes - VS Code Version: 1.118.0-insiders - OS Version: Windows 11 25R2 Steps to Reproduce: 1. Open VS Code Agents 2. Ask some copilot-type work 3. Observe that the "Thinking" content doesn't appear anymore 4. Observe that you can't see any of the tool calls anymore, no "Editing file", nothing This makes the entire app a black box, impossible to know what's happening at all. A couple days ago it had all the information I could need, I could open any tool calls and see the inputs/outputs of it and clearly understand what the LLM was doing by reading its internal thinking. Now this is not usable and I have to switch to the CLI again.

title: Terminal agent: send_to_terminal improvements for interactive programs
description:
## Problem

In terminalbench evaluation runs ([24890545491](https://github.com/meganrogge/vscode-copilot-evaluation/actions/runs/24890545491), [24890581356](https://github.com/meganrogge/vscode-copilot-evaluation/actions/runs/24890581356)), several failures were caused by `send_to_terminal` returning stale or insufficient output:

### Failure cases this addresses

| Task | Run | Issue |
|------|-----|-------|
| `blind-maze-explorer-5x5` | 24890545491 | Agent sends moves but only sees 5 lines of old output, misses game state |
| `play-zork` | 24890545491 | Agent interacts with text adventure but gets no response output back |
| `decode-braille` | 24890581356 | Agent sends to interactive program, gets stale output |

**~3 failures** directly caused by these limitations, with more failures likely influenced.

### Root cause

1. **Too few output lines**: `send_to_terminal` returned only 5 lines by default — insufficient for most interactive program responses
2. **Too short wait time**: 100ms wait before reading output was not enough for programs that take time to respond
3. **No idle-wait mode**: For interactive programs (games, REPLs), output arrives asynchronously. There was no way to wait for the program to finish responding before reading output
4. **No marker-scoped output**: Output was read from the entire terminal buffer rather than scoped to what appeared after the command was sent, causing stale output from previous commands to be returned

### Fix (on `merogge/send-to-terminal-tweaks`)

1. **Increased default output** from 5 → 20 lines
2. **Increased default wait** from 100ms → 2000ms
3. **Added `waitForOutput` parameter**: When `true`, waits for terminal to become idle (no new data for 2s) before returning output — critical for interactive programs
4. **Marker-scoped output**: Registers an xterm marker before sending text so output is scoped to just the response
5. **Updated model description** to tell the LLM about the 20-line default and `waitForOutput` option

### Schema change

```json
{
  "waitForOutput": {
    "type": "boolean",
    "description": "When true, waits for the terminal to become idle before returning output. Use for interactive programs."
  }
}
```

title: builtInExtensionsEnabledWithAutoUpdates causes copilot-chat to have two conflicting versions, crashing chat initialization
description:
## Bug: Built-in copilot-chat auto-update creates duplicate extension conflict

### Environment
- VS Code: 1.116.0, 1.117.0 (reproduced on both)
- OS: Windows 10/11
- Reproduced on: 6 separate machines (local, DevBox, tunnel-connected)

### Problem

Since VS Code 1.116, `GitHub.copilot-chat` ships as a **built-in extension** in `<install-dir>/resources/app/extensions/copilot/`. On every launch, the `builtInExtensionsEnabledWithAutoUpdates` array in `product.json` triggers VS Code to pull a newer version from the marketplace into `~/.vscode/extensions/`.

This creates **two active versions** of copilot-chat (e.g., built-in `0.45.0` + user `0.45.1`), which crashes the extension host with:

> "Chat took too long to get ready. Please ensure you are signed in to GitHub and that the extension `GitHub.copilot-chat` is installed and enabled."

### Root cause

`product.json` contains:
```json
"builtInExtensionsEnabledWithAutoUpdates": ["GitHub.copilot-chat"]
```

This is a **product-level auto-update mechanism** completely separate from the user setting `extensions.autoUpdate`. Setting `extensions.autoUpdate: false` has **zero effect** — the built-in auto-update still fires.

Evidence from shared process log:
```
"operation":3, "isApplicationScoped":true, "isBuiltin":true, "source":"gallery"
"Removed the extension from removed list: github.copilot-chat"
```

Even after manually uninstalling the user copy, VS Code removes it from the "removed" list and reinstalls it on next startup.

### Reproduction
1. Install VS Code 1.117.0 (stable)
2. Open any workspace — Copilot Chat works (built-in `0.45.0`)
3. Restart VS Code
4. VS Code auto-downloads `copilot-chat 0.45.1` into `~/.vscode/extensions/`
5. Extension host crashes → "Chat took too long" error

### Workaround

Patch `product.json` in the install directory (requires admin):
```json
"builtInExtensionsEnabledWithAutoUpdates": []
```
Then delete the user-installed copy and clean `extensions.json`.

**Problems with this workaround:**
- Requires admin privileges
- **Wiped on every VS Code update** (new build hash → new `product.json`)
- User-level `%APPDATA%\Code\product.json` override is ignored on some machines
- Tunnel/remote hosts have their own `product.json` that must be patched separately
- No user-accessible setting controls this behavior

### Expected behavior

Either:
1. The built-in auto-update should not create a conflicting second copy, OR
2. `extensions.autoUpdate: false` should also suppress `builtInExtensionsEnabledWithAutoUpdates`, OR
3. A user-facing setting should exist to disable built-in extension gallery updates

### Scope

This likely affects every VS Code user on 1.116+ where the gallery version is ahead of the built-in version. The hundreds of "Chat took too long" reports since 1.116 (#307751, #310923, #309101, #306614, #304499, #304084, etc.) may share this root cause.

### Confirmed on

| Machine type | VS Code | Built-in | Gallery | Fix applied |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Local Windows | 1.116.0 | 0.44.0 | 0.44.2 | admin product.json patch |
| Azure DevBox (3 machines) | 1.116.0 | 0.44.0 | 0.44.2 | admin patch + extensions.json cleanup |
| Tunnel host | 1.116.0 | 0.44.0 | 0.44.2 | server product.json patch |
| Local Windows | 1.117.0 | 0.45.0 | 0.45.1 | pending re-patch after update |

title: RunInTerminalTool hangs forever when trackIdleOnPrompt is stuck in Executing state
description:
## Bug

`trackIdleOnPrompt` in the execute strategy has a dead state: once the state machine enters `Executing` (on a `C`/`D` shell integration sequence), both the `scheduler` and `promptFallbackScheduler` are cancelled with no recovery path. If shell integration fails to emit the `A` (prompt) sequence after the command finishes, the tool hangs indefinitely.

This affects **any command where SI loses track of completion** — multiline commands sent via bracketed paste mode, heredocs, and long-running commands.

## Root Cause

In `trackIdleOnPrompt` ([executeStrategy.ts](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminalContrib/chatAgentTools/browser/executeStrategy/executeStrategy.ts)), the `onData` handler has this logic:

```typescript
if (state === TerminalState.PromptAfterExecuting) {
    promptFallbackScheduler.cancel();
    scheduler.schedule();
} else {
    scheduler.cancel();
    if (state === TerminalState.Initial || state === TerminalState.Prompt) {
        promptFallbackScheduler.schedule();
    } else {
        promptFallbackScheduler.cancel();  // ← kills fallback in Executing state
    }
}
```

And the `promptFallbackScheduler` callback has an early return:
```typescript
if (state === TerminalState.Executing || state === TerminalState.PromptAfterExecuting) {
    promptFallbackScheduler.cancel();
    return;  // ← even if it fires, does nothing in Executing state
}
```

Once `C`/`D` fires → state = `Executing` → both schedulers cancelled → no `A` sequence arrives → promise never resolves → tool hangs forever.

The `promptFallbackScheduler` was added in Nov 2025 (commit `25a53d905d5`, "prevent execute strategy from hanging") specifically to handle this, but it was gated to only work in `Initial`/`Prompt` states — not in `Executing`, which is where the actual hang happens.

## Evidence from Eval Run

Run `24890545491` (terminalbench, vscode agent v0.20260424.4) — 4 tests hung for the full 3600s timeout, all with `X_AGENT_STILL_RESPONDING`:

### Test 1: `cobol-modernization` — Same heredoc pattern, fast succeeds, slow hangs

3 earlier multiline/heredoc commands succeeded because they completed in <260ms (SI tracked them), but the 4th hung:

| Command | Duration | Lines | Result |
|---------|----------|-------|--------|
| `set -e; rm; mkdir; cp; cobc; ./bookforum; wc; python3 <<'PY'...PY` | **257ms** | 11 | ✅ SI tracked completion |
| `set -e; rm; mkdir; cp; printf; cobc; ./bookforum; python3 <<'PY'...PY` | **199ms** | 14 | ✅ SI tracked completion |
| `set -e; rm; mkdir; cp; python3 program.py; cobc; ./bookforum; cmp; cat` | **209ms** | 21 | ✅ SI tracked completion |
| `set -e; rm; mkdir; cp; printf; python3 program.py; cobc; ./bookforum; cmp; python3 <<'PY'...PY` | **∞ (hung)** | 26 | ❌ SI lost track |

```
terminal.log:
13:07:03.036 [info] Using `rich` execute strategy for command ` set -e\nrm -rf ...`
13:07:13.113 [warning] Shell integration failed to add capabilities within 10 seconds
(no further entries — hung until 3600s timeout)

agent-output.log:
X_AGENT_STILL_RESPONDING - Timeout of 3600000ms exceeded while waiting for chat command to complete.
```

### Test 2: `crack-7z-hash` — Same john command, one finishes, one doesn't

Two nearly identical `john` runs — the first succeeded because john exited (cracked the password), the second hung because john ran longer than the 3600s timeout:

| Command | Duration | Result |
|---------|----------|--------|
| `./john --format=7z --single --pot=...` | **6 min 25 sec** | ✅ john exited → `A` prompt emitted → state machine resolved |
| `./john --format=7z --wordlist=.../english.txt --rules=Wordlist --pot=...` | **∞ (hung)** | ❌ john still running → no `A` sequence → state machine stuck |

```
terminal.log:
13:10:12.970 [info] Using `rich` execute strategy for command ` ./john --format=7z ... --single ...`
13:10:23.046 [warning] Shell integration failed to add capabilities within 10 seconds
13:16:38.233 [info] Finished `rich` execute strategy with exitCode `0`  ← john exited after 6m25s

13:16:56.723 [info] Using `rich` execute strategy for command ` cd /app/john/run && ./john --format=7z ... --wordlist=...`
13:17:06.808 [warning] Shell integration failed to add capabilities within 10 seconds
(no further entries — hung until 3600s timeout)
```

### Test 3: `csv-to-parquet` — First and only command hung

```
terminal.log:
13:06:15.899 [info] Using `rich` execute strategy for command ` cd /app && set -e\nif command -v python3 ...; then\n  python3 - <<'PY'\n...\nPY\nelse\n...\nfi\nls -l /app/data.parquet`
13:06:25.975 [warning] Shell integration failed to add capabilities within 10 seconds
(no further entries)
```

### Test 4: `build-initramfs-qemu` — Multiline compound with gcc

2 prior commands succeeded (single-line 69ms, multiline 45ms), then:

```
terminal.log:
13:06:13.460 [info] Using `rich` execute strategy for command ` set -e\nprintf ... >/tmp/cp_test_static.c\ngcc -static -s -o /tmp/cp_test_static /tmp/cp_test_static.c\nfile /tmp/cp_test_static\nldd /bin/bash || true\nldd /bin/ls || true\nldd /usr/bin/mount || true`
13:06:23.570 [warning] Shell integration failed to add capabilities within 10 seconds
(no further entries)
```

### Common pattern across all 4

Every hanging test shows the exact same terminal.log signature:
1. `Using \`rich\` execute strategy for command ...` — command submitted
2. `Shell integration failed to add capabilities within 10 seconds` — SI lost track
3. **No further log entries** — state machine stuck in `Executing`, both schedulers cancelled, promise never resolves
4. After 3600s → `X_AGENT_STILL_RESPONDING` from the eval harness

## Fix

Two changes in `trackIdleOnPrompt`:

1. **Allow `promptFallbackScheduler` to act during `Executing` state** — remove `TerminalState.Executing` from the early-return guard in the callback
2. **Keep rescheduling `promptFallbackScheduler` on data events during `Executing` state** — remove the conditional cancel in the `onData` handler

This means: when no data flows for `promptFallbackMs` while in `Executing`, the fallback fires, transitions to `PromptAfterExecuting`, and the idle timer starts. If data resumes (command still producing output), the fallback keeps getting rescheduled — active commands with ongoing output are not terminated prematurely.

## Relationship to PR #307960

PR #307960 (merged Apr 24, 2026) fixed heredoc newline collapsing in `normalizeCommandForExecution`. That fix was already in the build for eval run `24890545491` — these 4 hangs occurred **with** the heredoc fix in place. The two issues are independent: #307960 ensures heredocs are sent correctly, this issue ensures the state machine recovers when SI can't detect command completion.

title: builtInExtensionsEnabledWithAutoUpdates causes copilot-chat to have two conflicting versions, crashing chat initialization
description:
## Bug: Built-in copilot-chat auto-update creates duplicate extension conflict

### Environment
- VS Code: 1.116.0, 1.117.0 (reproduced on both)
- OS: Windows 10/11
- Reproduced on: 6 separate machines (local, DevBox, tunnel-connected)

### Problem

Since VS Code 1.116, `GitHub.copilot-chat` ships as a **built-in extension** in `<install-dir>/resources/app/extensions/copilot/`. On every launch, the `builtInExtensionsEnabledWithAutoUpdates` array in `product.json` triggers VS Code to pull a newer version from the marketplace into `~/.vscode/extensions/`.

This creates **two active versions** of copilot-chat (e.g., built-in `0.45.0` + user `0.45.1`), which crashes the extension host with:

> "Chat took too long to get ready. Please ensure you are signed in to GitHub and that the extension `GitHub.copilot-chat` is installed and enabled."

### Root cause

`product.json` contains:
```json
"builtInExtensionsEnabledWithAutoUpdates": ["GitHub.copilot-chat"]
```

This is a **product-level auto-update mechanism** completely separate from the user setting `extensions.autoUpdate`. Setting `extensions.autoUpdate: false` has **zero effect** — the built-in auto-update still fires.

Evidence from shared process log:
```
"operation":3, "isApplicationScoped":true, "isBuiltin":true, "source":"gallery"
"Removed the extension from removed list: github.copilot-chat"
```

Even after manually uninstalling the user copy, VS Code removes it from the "removed" list and reinstalls it on next startup.

### Reproduction
1. Install VS Code 1.117.0 (stable)
2. Open any workspace — Copilot Chat works (built-in `0.45.0`)
3. Restart VS Code
4. VS Code auto-downloads `copilot-chat 0.45.1` into `~/.vscode/extensions/`
5. Extension host crashes → "Chat took too long" error

### Workaround

Patch `product.json` in the install directory (requires admin):
```json
"builtInExtensionsEnabledWithAutoUpdates": []
```
Then delete the user-installed copy and clean `extensions.json`.

**Problems with this workaround:**
- Requires admin privileges
- **Wiped on every VS Code update** (new build hash → new `product.json`)
- User-level `%APPDATA%\Code\product.json` override is ignored on some machines
- Tunnel/remote hosts have their own `product.json` that must be patched separately
- No user-accessible setting controls this behavior

### Expected behavior

Either:
1. The built-in auto-update should not create a conflicting second copy, OR
2. `extensions.autoUpdate: false` should also suppress `builtInExtensionsEnabledWithAutoUpdates`, OR
3. A user-facing setting should exist to disable built-in extension gallery updates

### Scope

This likely affects every VS Code user on 1.116+ where the gallery version is ahead of the built-in version. The hundreds of "Chat took too long" reports since 1.116 (#307751, #310923, #309101, #306614, #304499, #304084, etc.) may share this root cause.

### Confirmed on

| Machine type | VS Code | Built-in | Gallery | Fix applied |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Local Windows | 1.116.0 | 0.44.0 | 0.44.2 | admin product.json patch |
| Azure DevBox (3 machines) | 1.116.0 | 0.44.0 | 0.44.2 | admin patch + extensions.json cleanup |
| Tunnel host | 1.116.0 | 0.44.0 | 0.44.2 | server product.json patch |
| Local Windows | 1.117.0 | 0.45.0 | 0.45.1 | pending re-patch after update |

title: Chronicle: session_files and session_refs tables are always empty locally
description:
## Problem

The `session_files` and `session_refs` tables in the local Chronicle store contain zero rows despite the tracking code existing in `_handleToolSpan`. The schema description promises file edit tracking and PR/commit/issue references, causing the LLM to waste tool calls querying empty tables.

## Current code

`_handleToolSpan` in `sessionStoreTracker.ts` does extract file paths and refs from tool spans:
- `extractFilePath` handles `apply_patch`, `str_replace_editor`, `create_file`, `create` tools
- `extractRefsFromMcpTool` / `extractRefsFromTerminal` extract PR/issue/commit refs

## Likely causes

1. Tool spans may not carry the expected `gen_ai.tool.name` attribute, or the tool names don't match the tracked set (`apply_patch`, `str_replace_editor`, `create_file`, `create`).
2. Tool spans may not have a `session_id` attribute, causing `_getSessionId` to return undefined and skip tracking.
3. The buffer flush may not be writing files/refs rows correctly.

## Investigation steps

1. Add logging or check OTel debug panel to verify tool spans have `gen_ai.tool.name` and a session ID attribute.
2. Check whether the tool names used in VS Code Copilot match `FILE_TRACKING_TOOLS` in `sessionStoreTracking.ts`.
3. Verify the SQL INSERT for files/refs in the session store flush logic.

## Files

- `extensions/copilot/src/extension/chronicle/vscode-node/sessionStoreTracker.ts` — `_handleToolSpan`
- `extensions/copilot/src/extension/chronicle/common/sessionStoreTracking.ts` — `extractFilePath`, `extractRefsFromMcpTool`, `extractRefsFromTerminal`
- `extensions/copilot/src/platform/chronicle/common/sessionStore.ts` — flush/insert logic

title: Chronicle: populate agent_name on sessions from invoke_agent spans
description:
## Problem

`sessions.agent_name` is always empty in the local Chronicle store. The code in `_initSession` reads `GenAiAttr.AGENT_NAME` (`gen_ai.agent.name`) from the span, but this attribute is only set on **inference spans** (in `chatMLFetcher.ts` line 250), not on `invoke_agent` spans that trigger session creation.

## Current code

```typescript
// sessionStoreTracker.ts _initSession
const sessionSource = (span.attributes[GenAiAttr.AGENT_NAME] as string | undefined) ?? 'unknown';
this._bufferSessionUpsert({ id: sessionId, host_type: 'vscode', agent_name: sessionSource });
```

This always falls through to `'unknown'` because `invoke_agent` spans don't carry `gen_ai.agent.name`.

## Expected behavior

`agent_name` should identify the agent/mode that created the session (e.g. `'copilot'`, `'agent'`, `'edit'`, extension-contributed agents). The value is useful for the Chronicle intent to distinguish session types.

## Suggested approach

1. Check what attributes on `invoke_agent` spans carry the agent/mode name — likely `copilot_chat.agent_slug` or similar.
2. Update `_initSession` to read the correct attribute.
3. If no single attribute works, consider backfilling `agent_name` from child spans in `_backfillFromSpanAttributes`.
4. Add a test case to `sessionStoreTracker` or the common test suite.

## Files

- `extensions/copilot/src/extension/chronicle/vscode-node/sessionStoreTracker.ts` — `_initSession` method
- `extensions/copilot/src/platform/otel/common/genAiAttributes.ts` — attribute constants
- `extensions/copilot/src/extension/prompt/node/chatMLFetcher.ts` line 250 — where `AGENT_NAME` IS set (on inference spans)

Follow-up from #312292

title: Chronicle: sessions.summary contains raw JSON instead of human-readable text
description:
## Problem

`sessions.summary` often contains raw JSON blobs like `[{"type":"tool_result",…}]` instead of human-readable text. This makes `WHERE summary LIKE '%keyword%'` queries unreliable and confuses the Chronicle intent LLM.

## Current behavior

`_backfillFromSpanAttributes` sets `summary` from `CopilotChatAttr.USER_REQUEST`, truncated to 100 chars. Additionally, `_handleAgentSpan` sets summary from the first user message if no summary exists yet.

The issue is that `USER_REQUEST` or the first user message event content can itself be a raw JSON blob (e.g. tool results, structured messages), which gets stored as-is.

## Expected behavior

`summary` should be a short human-readable description of the session. If the first user message is structured/JSON, it should either:
- Be skipped in favor of a later plain-text message, or
- Have the text content extracted from the JSON structure

## Files

- `extensions/copilot/src/extension/chronicle/vscode-node/sessionStoreTracker.ts` — `_backfillFromSpanAttributes` and `_handleAgentSpan`
- `extensions/copilot/src/extension/intents/node/chronicleIntent.ts` — schema warns "summary may contain raw JSON"

Follow-up from #312292

title: Chronicle: local schema description drifted from actual SQLite data
description:
The `_getSchemaDescription()` prompt in `chronicleIntent.ts` documents column semantics that don't match the actual data stored in the local SQLite session database. This causes the LLM to write queries expecting data that isn't there, leading to empty/misleading results.

## Findings (validated against live local DB)

### `sessions` table

| Column | Schema says | Actual |
|---|---|---|
| `cwd` | Working directory | **Always empty string** — never populated |
| `host_type` | Listed as a column | Populated (e.g. `"vscode"`) — works correctly |
| `agent_name` | `'vscode'`, `'cli'`, `'CCA'`, `'CCR'` | **Always empty string** — the role it claims is actually filled by `host_type` |
| `agent_description` | Listed as a column | **Always empty string** |
| `summary` | Session summary text | Contains **raw JSON blobs** (`[{"type":"tool_result",…}]`) or empty — not human-readable |
| `repository` | Repo URL | ✅ Populated correctly |
| `branch` | Branch name | ✅ Populated correctly |

### `turns` table

| Column | Schema says | Actual |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | **Not documented** | Exists as auto-increment PK |
| `user_message` | User prompts | ✅ Populated correctly |
| `assistant_response` | Assistant replies | **Always empty string** — never populated |
| `session_id`, `turn_index`, `timestamp` | As documented | ✅ Correct |

### `session_files` / `session_refs` tables

Both tables exist but contain **zero rows** — no file edits or PR/commit/issue references are being tracked locally.

## Impact

- The LLM is told `agent_name` distinguishes session creators (`'vscode'`, `'cli'`, etc.) and writes `WHERE agent_name = 'vscode'` queries that return nothing.
- The schema says `assistant_response` "contains the assistant's replies" — prompting the LLM to analyze response quality, which is impossible since the column is always empty.
- The `summary` field is described as usable text but contains unparsed JSON, making `WHERE summary LIKE '%keyword%'` queries unreliable.
- `session_files` and `session_refs` are documented as populated tables, so the LLM wastes tool-call iterations querying empty tables.

## Suggested fixes

1. Add caveats to the local schema noting that `cwd`, `agent_name`, `agent_description`, and `assistant_response` are often empty locally.
2. Note that `summary` may contain raw JSON and is not reliable for text search — recommend JOINing with `turns.user_message` instead (similar to the existing cloud schema caveat).
3. Consider noting that `session_files` and `session_refs` may be empty, to avoid wasted tool calls.
4. Investigate whether `assistant_response` and `agent_name` should be populated by the indexing pipeline.

**File:** `extensions/copilot/src/extension/intents/node/chronicleIntent.ts` — `_getSchemaDescription()` (local branch, ~line 414)

title: chat/subagent: Provide API to control default expanded state of subagent content parts
description: Problem When a chat participant or custom agent delegates work to a subagent via runSubagent, the subagent's output (tool calls, progress, file reads/writes) is rendered in a collapsible section that is collapsed by default. User impact: Because the subagent section is collapsed, users see no visible activity while the subagent is running — no file reads, no tool calls, no incremental progress. This makes the chat panel appear frozen or stuck. Users have no indication that work is progressing and frequently assume the agent has hung, leading them to cancel or restart the session prematurely. This is especially damaging for long-running multi-step workflows where each phase may take tens of seconds or minutes. There is currently no API surface (neither in the stable [vscode](vscode-file://vscode-app/Applications/Visual%20Studio%20Code.app/Contents/Resources/app/out/vs/code/electron-browser/workbench/workbench.html) API nor in the proposed [vscode.proposed.chatParticipantAdditions.d.ts](vscode-file://vscode-app/Applications/Visual%20Studio%20Code.app/Contents/Resources/app/out/vs/code/electron-browser/workbench/workbench.html)) that allows an extension to control whether a subagent section should start expanded or collapsed. Expected Behavior Extensions that invoke subagents should be able to opt into showing progress expanded by default, so users can observe what the subagent is doing in real time without having to manually click to expand.

Tests for adding `/remote` flow for Copilot CLI sessions, similar to what's available directly in Copilot CLI.

- Enable `github.copilot.chat.cli.remote.enabled`.
- Open a GitHub-backed workspace folder.

### Test: Enable remote control
1. Run `/remote` in the Copilot CLI session.
2. Verify chat shows "Enabling remote control..." followed by a persistent banner that remote control is enabled.
3. Verify an **Open on GitHub** button appears.
4. Open the GitHub task page.

### Test: Approve from GitHub
1. Ask the session to run a shell command that requires approval.
2. Verify approval UI appears in VS Code and on GitHub.
3. Approve on GitHub.
4. Verify the tool call starts in VS Code and the local approval prompt is dismissed.
5. Verify subsequent output is mirrored to GitHub.

### Test: Approve from VS Code
1. Trigger another permission-requiring tool call while `/remote` is active.
2. Approve it in VS Code.

4. Verify the tool execution and output still appear on GitHub.

### Test: Running state and disconnect
1. Trigger a command or tool that shows running state on GitHub.
2. Verify the GitHub task page shows the session as running while work is in progress.
3. Wait for completion and verify the running state clears when the session becomes idle.
4. Run `/remote off`.
5. Send another prompt.
6. Verify new turns remain local to VS Code and are no longer mirrored to GitHub.

### Test: Failure cases
1. Run `/remote` with the setting disabled; verify chat explains the command is experimental and disabled.
2. Run `/remote` in a non-GitHub workspace; verify chat explains that the workspace is not a GitHub repository.
3. Run `/remote` without the required GitHub permissions; verify chat surfaces that additional GitHub permissions are required.

title: Chat session history: session_files and session_refs tables are never populated
description:
## Bug

The `session_files` and `session_refs` tables in the local chat session history store are always empty (0 rows), even across 460+ sessions with active file editing and tool use.

## Repro

1. Use Copilot Chat (agent mode or panel) in VS Code over multiple sessions — edit files, create files, reference PRs/issues
2. Query the local session history store:
   ```sql
   SELECT COUNT(*) FROM session_files;  -- returns 0
   SELECT COUNT(*) FROM session_refs;   -- returns 0
   ```
3. Meanwhile, `sessions` (462 rows) and `turns` (rich tool call content) are populated normally

## Expected

`session_files` should track files read/edited/created by tool calls during chat sessions. `session_refs` should track linked PRs, issues, commits, etc.

## Evidence

title: execution_subagent internal "Execution query:" framing leaks into session turn logs
description:
When the `execution_subagent` tool is invoked, `ExecutionSubagentTool.invoke()` prepends the literal string `"Execution query: \n"` to the user's query before passing it as a conversation turn to the subagent loop:

https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/extensions/copilot/src/extension/tools/node/executionSubagentTool.ts#L44-L47

```ts
const executionInstruction = [
    'Execution query: ',
    `${options.input.query}`,
    '',
].join('\n');
```

This internal framing string then appears verbatim in session transcript / turn logs (visible in the `turns` table as `user_message`), making it look like the user typed `"Execution query: …"`. This causes downstream consumers (e.g. chronicle/analytics prompts that summarize session history) to misattribute these as user prompts, skewing usage analysis.

**Expected:** Internal subagent framing should either be filtered from session transcripts or clearly tagged with metadata (e.g. `source: 'subagent'`) so transcript consumers can distinguish user-authored turns from system-injected turns.

title: Chronicle: session_refs table is always empty — ref tracking only fires for MCP tools and Copilot terminal spans
description:
## Problem

The Chronicle `session_refs` table is effectively always empty for typical VS Code workflows. Out of 452 sessions in my local store over 7 days, **0 have any refs tracked**.

The ref tracking heuristic in `sessionStoreTracker.ts` only captures references from two narrow sources:

1. **GitHub MCP server tool calls** (`github-mcp-server-*` prefix) — requires the GitHub MCP server to be active
2. **Copilot terminal tool spans** (`runInTerminal` / `run_in_terminal`) — only fires when `gh pr create`, `gh issue create`, or `git commit` are run **through Copilot's own terminal tool**, not in the user's regular terminal

This means:
- **SCM UI commits** (clicking the commit button in the Source Control view) — **not tracked**
- **Terminal commits** (`git commit` in the user's own integrated terminal) — **not tracked**
- **`gh pr` commands** run outside Copilot's tool — **not tracked**
- **Issue references in user prompts** (e.g., "Fix the bug from #87") — **not tracked**

## Impact

The `/chronicle standup` prompt renders `No references found.` for the `### References (PRs, Issues, Commits)` section virtually 100% of the time, making it unable to link sessions to PRs/issues/commits. The `session_refs` table and the standup prompt's ref section are dead code in practice.

## Root Cause

### `_handleToolSpan` in `sessionStoreTracker.ts` (line ~248)

```typescript
// Track refs from GitHub MCP server tools
if (isGitHubMcpTool(toolName)) {
    const refs = extractRefsFromMcpTool(toolName, toolArgs);
    ...
}

// Track refs from terminal/shell tool
if (toolName === 'runInTerminal' || toolName === 'run_in_terminal') {
    const refs = extractRefsFromTerminal(toolArgs, resultText);
    ...
}
```

There is **no integration with the Git extension's `onDidCommit` event**, which is already available in the VS Code Git API (`extensions/git/src/api/git.d.ts:237`) and is already consumed by the Copilot extension itself in `gitCommitMessageServiceImpl.ts` for commit message survival telemetry.

### `extractRefsFromTerminal` in `sessionStoreTracking.ts` (line ~96)

The regex patterns are intentionally narrow:
- `gh pr create` is matched, but `gh pr merge`, `gh pr edit` don't capture refs unless the specific subcommand is listed
- Only matches `git commit`, not `git merge`, `git cherry-pick`, `git revert` which also produce commit SHAs
- No extraction of issue/PR references from user prompt text (e.g., "Fix #123")

## Proposed Improvements

### P0 — Hook into Git extension's `onDidCommit` event
The `Repository.onDidCommit` event fires for **all** commits (SCM UI, terminal, CLI). After the event fires, `repository.state.HEAD?.commit` has the new SHA. This would capture the vast majority of missing commit refs.

The Copilot extension already uses this event in `gitCommitMessageServiceImpl.ts`:
```typescript
repository.onDidCommit(() => this._onDidCommit(repository), this);
```

A similar listener in `SessionStoreTracker` could:
1. Get the new commit SHA from `repository.state.HEAD.commit`
2. Correlate it to the most recently active session
3. Insert a `commit` ref

### P1 — Extract issue/PR references from user prompt text
Parse `#123`, `GH-123`, or full GitHub URLs from the user's prompt text in `_handleAgentSpan` and insert refs.

### P2 — Broaden terminal command patterns
- Add `git merge`, `git cherry-pick`, `git revert` to the commit SHA extraction regex
- Add `gh pr edit`, `gh pr close`, `gh pr review` to PR extraction

## Relevant Files

- `extensions/copilot/src/extension/chronicle/vscode-node/sessionStoreTracker.ts` — main tracker
- `extensions/copilot/src/extension/chronicle/common/sessionStoreTracking.ts` — extraction helpers
- `extensions/copilot/src/extension/chronicle/common/standupPrompt.ts` — standup prompt that consumes refs
- `extensions/copilot/src/platform/chronicle/common/sessionStore.ts` — RefRow type / ISessionStore interface
- `extensions/copilot/src/extension/prompt/vscode-node/gitCommitMessageServiceImpl.ts` — existing `onDidCommit` usage pattern
- `extensions/git/src/api/git.d.ts` — Git extension API with `onDidCommit` event

title: Chronicle analysis counts subagent sessions as single-turn usage
description:
Chronicle's usage analysis misclassifies subagent-spawned sessions as "single-turn sessions," inflating the single-turn percentage and misrepresenting user behavior.

**Root cause**: When a parent session spawns subagents (code review, code search, plan verification), each subagent gets its own session row. These sessions naturally have only 1 turn, but they are not independent user actions — they are tool calls from a multi-turn parent session.

**How to detect subagents**: Subagent session IDs use the Anthropic tool-use ID format (`toolu_bdrk_...`) instead of standard UUIDs. In my last 7 days: 192 of 447 sessions (43%) were subagents, but they all got counted as "single-turn" usage.

**Impact**: The analysis reported 76% single-turn sessions and recommended reducing throwaway sessions — when in reality most of those were automated subagent work from sophisticated multi-turn workflows.

**Suggested fix**: Filter or group subagent sessions (by ID format or a dedicated column) and attribute their activity to the parent session in usage summaries.

title: run_in_terminal returns partial output for multi-line POSIX commands (RichExecuteStrategy resolves on first onCommandFinished)
description:
## Summary

When the chat agent pastes a multi-line POSIX command via `run_in_terminal` (for example a `python - <<'PY' … PY` heredoc or a small `set -e; apt-get update; apt-get install -y …` script), the tool returns to the model after only the first line has run. The remaining lines continue executing in the terminal unattended while the agent moves on, causing empty/partial output, wasted follow-up turns, and incorrect patches.

## Root cause

[`RichExecuteStrategy.execute()`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminalContrib/chatAgentTools/browser/executeStrategy/richExecuteStrategy.ts) resolves on the **first** `onCommandFinished` shell-integration marker:

```ts
Event.toPromise(this._commandDetection.onCommandFinished, store).then(e => { ... })
```

Shell integration fires one marker per top-level statement. For a multi-line submission this means the strategy returns after line 1, even though the combined submission is logically a single tool call. Input detection in `OutputMonitor` is unaffected (it reads the PTY directly), so interactive prompts still surface — but command completion semantics are wrong.

### When was this introduced?

The behavior has been present since the rich execute strategy was first wired up to shell integration in commit `dfbea4a6a4a` "Get rich strat working" (2025-07-14) and `072f9f7d042` "Use command detection output and exit code". It was masked in practice by the nohup-compound corruption (#312202) for background commands; with that fixed, multi-line foreground heredocs now dominate the failure signal.

## Impact

Observed on eval run `24857589683` (terminalbench2, vscode agent). At least 8 of 25 failing instances trace directly to this bug, including:

- `bn-fit-modify`, `distribution-search`, `gcode-to-text`, `protein-assembly`, `raman-fitting`, `rstan-to-pystan`, `regex-chess`, `schemelike-metacircular-eval`

Each of those produced an empty or near-empty patch (`patch=0B`) after burning the model's token budget on spurious system-initiated follow-up turns triggered by early command completion.

title: Agents: Support sub-sessions (plus button) for Claude
description:
## Summary

The "New Sub-Session" plus button in the Agents window titlebar is currently gated by `capabilities.supportsMultipleChats`, which is only set to `true` for Copilot CLI sessions. Claude sessions always return `false`, so the button never appears.

## How Sub-Sessions Work Today (Copilot CLI)

The sub-session mechanism is a two-phase design in `copilotChatSessionsProvider.ts`:

1. **Pre-commit grouping** — when the plus button is pressed, a new `CopilotCLISession` stub is created with:
   - `setIsolationMode('workspace')` — reuses the parent's worktree
   - `setOption('parentSessionId', <parent resource path>)` — links the new stub to its parent in-memory so the Sessions list groups them immediately

2. **Post-commit persistence** — after the CLI agent materializes the real session, the CLI extension writes `metadata.sessionParentId` onto the committed session. On the next `getSessions()` call (including app restart), grouping is reconstructed by reading `agentSession.metadata.sessionParentId`.

Without `sessionParentId` in the committed session's metadata, sub-sessions group correctly within a single app session but **lose their grouping on restart**.

## What's Needed for Claude

### VS Code side (`copilotChatSessionsProvider.ts`)

1. **`_createNewSessionFrom`** — remove the `throw` for Claude and add a Claude branch that creates a `ClaudeCodeNewSession` with `setOption('parentSessionId', ...)`. Since Claude only supports workspace isolation (no worktrees yet), no `setIsolationMode` call is needed.

2. **`capabilities.supportsMultipleChats`** — extend the condition to include `ClaudeCodeSessionType`:
   ```ts
   capabilities: {
       supportsMultipleChats: (
           primaryChat.sessionType === CopilotCLISessionType.id ||
           primaryChat.sessionType === ClaudeCodeSessionType.id
       ) && this._isMultiChatEnabled()
   }
   ```

3. **`_chatToSingleChatSession`** — same condition for Claude sessions routed through the single-chat path.

### Claude Code extension side

The Claude extension needs to read the `parentSessionId` option forwarded with the chat request and stamp it onto the committed session's `metadata.sessionParentId` — otherwise sub-session grouping won't survive a restart.

## Note: Consider Waiting for Agent Host Protocol

It may be worth evaluating whether to implement this before or after the agent-host-protocol integration lands. If the protocol provides a first-class concept for session grouping/parenting, it could supersede the current `sessionParentId` metadata approach and make this work more straightforward (or unnecessary as a custom implementation).

Worktree isolation for Claude sub-sessions (matching the CLI experience) is also not yet supported but is planned for the future.

title: Warn the model when run_in_terminal leaves the workspace root (cwd drift)
description:
## Problem

When the agent uses `run_in_terminal` to `cd` into a directory outside the workspace root (e.g. `/tmp/...`) and does the bulk of its work there, downstream tools that inspect the workspace miss that work. Concretely:

- `git diff` rooted at the workspace produces an empty `patch.diff`.
- Evaluation harnesses that run assertions in a clean container against the workspace path cannot find files/services the agent set up.

This showed up as a regression in a terminalbench eval run (task: `git-multibranch`). The agent successfully built and verified a full git+nginx+TLS setup under `/tmp/final-test`, but `patch.diff` was 0 bytes and the test harness hit `TEST_TIMEOUT` (90s) because nothing the agent produced lived under the workspace root (`/app`).

CLI run (pass): `.vscode-eval/24800813436`  
VS Code run (fail): `.vscode-eval/24853453680/terminalbench.eval.x86_64.git-multibranch-output/output`

Evidence:
- `test_result.json`: `"failure_mode": "TEST_TIMEOUT"`
- `vsc-output/patch.diff`: 0 bytes
- Trajectory step 32: agent operating in `/tmp/final-test`, never persists to `/app`

## Proposal

In `run_in_terminal`'s tool-result builder (`runInTerminalTool.ts`), after every command, check the shell's end cwd against the workspace folders. When the cwd is outside all workspace folders (and at least one folder is open), append a short model-visible hint:

> Note: The shell's current directory (`<path>`) is outside the workspace root. Files written here may not be captured by tools that inspect the workspace.

This does not change execution — it only nudges the model to either `cd` back or explicitly persist output into the workspace. A first implementation has landed in the tool:

```ts
if (endCwd && this._workspaceContextService.getWorkspaceFolder(endCwd) === null) {
    const folders = this._workspaceContextService.getWorkspace().folders;
    if (folders.length > 0) {
        resultText.push(`\nNote: The shell's current directory (${endCwd.fsPath}) is outside the workspace root. ...\n`);
    }
}
```

## Considerations / follow-ups

- Should be a one-shot hint per drifted command, not spammed on every subsequent in-drift command (potential improvement: only emit on the *transition* from in-root → out-of-root).
- For multi-root workspaces, `getWorkspaceFolder` already covers all roots, so the hint only fires when truly outside all of them.
- No hint when no workspace folder is open (e.g. file-only windows) — behavior preserved.
- Consider a complementary telemetry field (`workdirDrift: boolean`) on the tool metadata so eval dashboards can surface this failure mode distinctly from assertion failures.

## Related

- PR #312180 (prompt-regex fix) addressed a different but related symptom: spurious "waiting for input" notices that sent the agent into polling loops.
- This issue covers the second regression pattern from the same eval comparison.

title: Chat code blocks no longer fire workspace.onDidOpenTextDocument (regression - breaks language features in chat)
description:
Chat code blocks (`vscode-chat-code-block:/...` and `vscode-copilot-chat-code-block:/...`) used to be visible to the extension host as `vscode.TextDocument`s, so language clients (Pylance, TS, etc.) received `textDocument/didOpen` and could provide hovers, completions, diagnostics, etc. inside rendered code blocks.

This stopped working. Pylance's `onDidOpenTextDocument` is no longer called for Copilot-generated Python code blocks, even though its `documentSelector` still includes both schemes.

### Root cause

In `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/widget/chatListRenderer.ts`:

```ts
this._editorPool     = this._register(this.instantiationService.createInstance(EditorPool, editorOptions, delegate, overflowWidgetsDomNode, true));
this._toolEditorPool = this._register(this.instantiationService.createInstance(EditorPool, editorOptions, delegate, overflowWidgetsDomNode, true));
```

The 4th arg is `isSimpleWidget`. It's now `true` for both pools (the constructor default is `false`).

`EditorPool` → `CodeBlockPart` → `IModelService.createModel(value, lang, uri, /*isForSimpleWidget*/ true)`. With `isForSimpleWidget=true`, the model is not mirrored to the extension host, so:

- no `vscode.TextDocument` is created
- `workspace.onDidOpenTextDocument` does not fire
- `vscode-languageclient` never sends `textDocument/didOpen`
- all ext-host language features (Pylance, TS, etc.) are silently disabled inside chat code blocks

### Repro

1. Open a Python workspace with the Pylance/Python extensions installed.
2. Ask Copilot Chat for a Python snippet.
3. Observe that Pylance's server never receives a `textDocument/didOpen` for the rendered code block (no hover, completions, diagnostics inside the block).

### Ask

Either revert these two pools to `isSimpleWidget: false`, or expose a way to keep chat code blocks ext-host-visible while retaining whatever simple-widget benefit motivated the flip.

This is a regression that affects every language extension that wants to participate in chat code blocks, not just Pylance.

Issue Summary

OpenRouter BYOK-related models continue to appear in the VS Code model picker even after I tried to remove them, and I do not use Settings Sync, so this does not appear to be coming from synced settings.

What I checked

I inspected the normal local user configuration on Windows and did not find any active OpenRouter configuration:

I then searched the broader VS Code Insiders user-data area. The only matches I found were in chat/session history and logs, which show that OpenRouter had been used previously. I did not find an obvious live config entry that explains why those models still appear in the picker.

Expected Behavior

If OpenRouter BYOK models are no longer configured, they should disappear from the model picker.

Actual Behavior

The OpenRouter-related models still appear in the model picker even though:

Settings Sync is disabled
local model config is empty
local user settings do not contain OpenRouter/BYOK config
no active OpenRouter/BYOK entries were found in standard local storage

This looks like stale model/provider state being cached somewhere outside the normal user settings flow, possibly in extension state or remote/WSL-side VS Code server state, rather than in local Windows settings.

Why this seems like a VS Code bug

From a user perspective, there is no discoverable place to remove these model entries once they have been introduced. If the picker is backed by cached provider state, that state either:

is not being cleared when config is removed, or
is being loaded from a hidden location that is not surfaced to the user

title: Allow folders with skills shipped via extensions to be read without user confirmations
description:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

<!-- Describe the feature you'd like. -->
Our dotnet modernization agent shipped as extension and ships a lot of skills with it. They are discovered and matched for tasks dynamically by our agent tools. For VS code they are just some files on disk - they are not in the user repo or user profile skill location, so for VS code they are not "skills". We make them to be like default skills via our instructions and LLM does read them as skills later - however user sees confirmations when a skill A folder is read first time. 

We need a way for our extension to specify that all those files (a root folder) is trusted since it is shipped by us and read_file tool does not ask for confirmation.

title: Background terminal monitor fires spurious "needs input" notifications for streaming commands
description:
## Summary

The background terminal output monitor surfaces `` `<command>` needs input `` steering notifications for commands that are not actually waiting for user input. Observed with commands like:

- `cd <dir> && npx hereby test`
- `cd <dir> && npx hereby format && go test ./internal/ls ./internal/lsp/... ./internal/fourslash/... 2>&1 | tail -20 && npx hereby lint 2>&1 | tail -10`
- `go test ./...`
- `npx hereby lint 2>&1 | tail -10`

The notification fires repeatedly while the command continues producing output, derailing the agent with bogus steering messages.

## Reproduction

1. Have the agent invoke a long-running, streaming command whose output contains lines ending with `:` or `?` followed by a newline (e.g. `Running tests:`, `Summary:`, log output with a trailing `?`).
2. Observe the `needs input` notification firing in the background while the command is still running.

## Root cause

Three compounding changes in `src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminalContrib/chatAgentTools/browser/tools/monitoring/outputMonitor.ts` and `runInTerminalTool.ts`:

1. **Overly loose regexes in `detectsInputRequiredPattern`** (introduced in #263901, Aug 2025). Patterns like `/:\s*$/`, `/\?\s*$/i`, `/\(y\)\s*$/i`, and `/password[:]?$/i` match any buffer tail ending with `:\n`, `?\n`, etc. — which is typical of normal command output, not actual prompts. `\s*` also matches `\n`, so a header line followed by a newline matches.

2. **Removal of LLM second-pass filter** (#308587, Apr 9, 2026 — "remove LLM calls to detect prompts for input, add fg terminal support for send_to_terminal/get_terminal_output"). Previously a regex hit only suggested an input prompt; an LLM call confirmed it before surfacing anything. After this PR, raw regex results drive behavior directly, so all false positives leak through.

3. **Continuous background monitoring + steering notifications** (#307199, Apr 2, 2026 — "Add completion notifications and async prompt monitoring for background terminals"). Added `continueMonitoringAsync`, which keeps re-running idle detection and pattern matching for the lifetime of a background command, and wired `onDidDetectInputNeeded` into `IChatService.sendRequest` with ``systemInitiatedLabel: "`{0}` needs input"``. Before this, input detection effectively ran once per command; now every transient idle window during a long-running command is a new chance to fire.

None of these alone caused user-visible issues, but together they produce the bug: a long-running streaming command hits a momentary idle window, the tail happens to end with `:\n` or `?\n`, the loose regex matches, no LLM filter vetoes it, and the background monitor fires a steering notification.

## Fix

Tighten `detectsInputRequiredPattern` to require **a trailing space** after prompt punctuation. Real interactive prompts position the cursor one space past the punctuation (`"Continue? "`, `"Password: "`) so that typed characters don't abut the prompt. Non-prompt output ends with a newline when the program moves on to the next line.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| `/:\s*$/` | `/: +$/` |
| `/\?\s*(?:\([a-z\s]+\))?$/i` | `/\? *(?:\([a-z\s]+\))? +$/i` |
| `/\(y\)\s*$/i` | `/\(y\) +$/i` |
| `/password[:]?$/i` | `/password:? +$/i` |
| `/:\s*\([^)]*\)\s*$/` | `/:\s*\([^)]*\) +$/` |

The PowerShell multi-option pattern, yes/no pair patterns, `(END)`, and `press any key` patterns already required trailing whitespace or were specific enough and are unchanged.

## Impact

**Fixes:** Spurious `needs input` notifications for normal streaming commands whose output tail transiently ends with `:`, `?`, `(y)`, or `password` followed by a newline — including `go test`, `hereby`, `eslint`, `npm test | tail`, log tailers, CI runners, build scripts.

**Preserves:** All real prompts where the cursor rests after a trailing space — the canonical form for interactive TTY prompts (readline, `getpass`, PowerShell `Read-Host`, npm/git prompts).

**Trade-off:** A prompt rendered without a trailing space (e.g. `"Continue?"` with the cursor immediately after `?`) will no longer be auto-detected. This is rare in practice and strictly preferable to the current high false-positive rate; the agent can still react to real prompts via `get_terminal_output`.

**Title:** Remote SSH: Copilot/agent plugin discovery fails with `PendingMigrationError: navigator is now a global in nodejs` on VS Code 1.117.0

Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: N/A

- VS Code Version: 1.117.0
- OS Version:
  - Local: macOS
  - Remote SSH target: Linux
  - Remote VS Code Server Node: v22.22.1

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Open VS Code 1.117.0 and connect to a Linux machine using Remote SSH.
2. Open a workspace with Copilot Chat enabled.
3. Enable agent plugins and configure `chat.plugins.marketplaces` with a valid marketplace repository.
4. Open Extensions and search for `@agentPlugins`.
5. Observe that plugin discovery in the UI is incomplete or unreliable.
6. Check the remote extension host logs.

Observed result:

The remote extension host logs show:

```text
PendingMigrationError: navigator is now a global in nodejs, please see https://aka.ms/vscode-extensions/navigator for additional info on this error.
    at get (.../extensionHostProcess.js:831:7210)
    at .../server/extensions/copilot/dist/extension.js:...
```

The error occurs while the bundled Copilot extension is loading in the remote extension host. In this state, the agent plugin UI does not reliably load the configured marketplace contents.

Expected result:

Copilot should activate cleanly in Remote SSH sessions without throwing `PendingMigrationError`, and the `@agentPlugins` UI should load the full contents of the configured marketplace.

Additional information:

- This does not appear to be a marketplace or plugin manifest issue.
- I validated the same marketplace on the same remote machine using the standalone `copilot` CLI.
- The CLI successfully browses all expected plugins from the same marketplace, which suggests the repo structure and manifests are valid.
- The issue appears specific to the VS Code Remote SSH runtime path when the bundled Copilot extension activates.

Validation used on the remote machine:

```bash
copilot --config-dir /tmp/copilot-test-config plugin marketplace add /home/user/extreme-agent-plugins
copilot --config-dir /tmp/copilot-test-config plugin marketplace browse extreme-agent-plugins
```

That command successfully listed all expected plugins from the marketplace, confirming the repo structure and manifests are valid.

### The Issue
Currently, when using the VS Code Speech extension with Copilot Chat, the interaction follows a "walkie-talkie" model. As soon as the microphone button is released, the captured text is immediately sent to the chat.

This is problematic because sometimes I would like to edit the prompt (correct some mistakes in the transcript, add some context, etc.)

### Feature I'd like
I would like a setting or a toggle to bypass the "Walkie-Talkie" mode. Specifically: an option where releasing the dictation button places the text into the Chat input field but does not trigger the "Enter" (send) command.

### Alternatives considered
Currently, the only workaround is to use system-level dictation (e.g., Win+H on Windows or Cmd+Dictation on Mac), but this doesn't leverage the seamless integration of VS Code Speech extension.

title: Insiders Update Fails - Windows - MoveFile failed; code 5. Access is denied
description: Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: No (issue is with the auto-updater, not the editor itself) - VS Code Version: Insiders ``` Version: 1.118.0-insider (user setup) Commit: 102df5b59f1c706f14aee2259d4ec60a6acee55c Date: 2026-04-22T11:25:25Z Electron: 39.8.8 ElectronBuildId: 13870025 Chromium: 142.0.7444.265 Node.js: 22.22.1 V8: 14.2.231.22-electron.0 OS: Windows_NT x64 10.0.26200 ``` - OS Version: Windows 11 Pro 25H2 (10.0.26200), single user, non-managed, no MDM/Group Policy ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Have VS Code Insiders installed per-user (`C:\Users\\AppData\Local\Programs\Microsoft VS Code Insiders`) 2. Allow VS Code Insiders to detect and attempt an automatic update (Help → Check for Updates) 3. Observe the error dialog: **"An error occurred while trying to rename a file in the destination directory: MoveFile failed; code 5. Access is denied."** pointing to a `.pak` file in the new commit subfolder (e.g. `102df5b59f\chrome_100_percent.pak`) ## What Happens The auto-updater downloads the update successfully and completes the file removal phase without errors (confirmed via `vscode-inno-updater-*.log` in `%TEMP%`). The failure occurs when the updater spawns the Inno Setup installer as a subprocess to extract the new version. The Inno Setup log (`%TEMP%\Setup Log *.txt`) shows the installer is being launched with **no privileges**: ``` 2026-04-22 10:14:23.159 Compatibility mode: Yes (RunAsInvoker) 2026-04-22 10:14:23.159 User privileges: None ``` A normal per-user install should show `User privileges: Standard`. The `RunAsInvoker` compatibility mode causes the subprocess to inherit a restricted token from the VS Code parent process, stripping it of the permissions needed to write to its own install directory — even though the user is the owner of that directory. The full Inno Setup installer command spawned by the updater: ``` CodeSetup-insider-.exe /verysilent /log /update="..." /progress="..." /sessionend="..." /cancel="..." /nocloseapplications /mergetasks=runcode,!desktopicon,!quicklaunchicon ``` The installer retries `MoveFile` four times before giving up: ``` 2026-04-22 10:14:24.404 MoveFile: The existing file appears to be in use (5). Retrying. 2026-04-22 10:14:25.410 MoveFile: The existing file appears to be in use (5). Retrying. 2026-04-22 10:14:26.417 MoveFile: The existing file appears to be in use (5). Retrying. 2026-04-22 10:14:27.424 MoveFile: The existing file appears to be in use (5). Retrying. 2026-04-22 10:14:28.439 Message box (Abort/Retry/Ignore): MoveFile failed; code 5. Access is denied. ``` The target file does not exist prior to the install attempt — this is not a file-locking issue. The failure is a permissions issue caused by the restricted token. ## What is Expected The auto-updater completes successfully. The Inno Setup subprocess should run with `User privileges: Standard`, not `User privileges: None`. ## Key Finding Running the downloaded installer manually from `%TEMP%\vscode-insider-user-x64\CodeSetup-insider-.exe` as the **same user** completes successfully without any errors. This confirms the issue is specific to how VS Code spawns the Inno Setup subprocess via `RunAsInvoker`, causing it to inherit a restricted token. ## What Workarounds Were Attempted - Full uninstall and reinstall — issue recurs on next update cycle - Remove %APPDATA%\Code - Insiders directory - Remove %USERPROFILE%\.vscode-agents-insiders directory - `takeown` and `icacls /reset` on the install directory - Clearing `%TEMP%\SquirrelTemp` - Disabling Windows Defender real-time protection - Killing all integrated terminals before updating - Closing and freshly reopening VS Code before triggering update - Adjusting UAC `ConsentPromptBehaviorAdmin` registry value - No third-party AV, no MDM/Group Policy, no VS Code scheduled tasks present ## Workaround Setting `"update.mode": "manual"` in settings and downloading the installer directly from https://code.visualstudio.com/insiders/ works reliably, as does running the downloaded installer manually from the temp folder.

I would like `extensions.json` to automatically capture all extensions that are currently configured in my workspace.  This will help all developers in a team have the same user experience. 
Let me explain the context.

<!-- Failed to upload "image.png" -->

## Background
We understand that VS Code has been architected as a generic IDE. You can simply install whatever extensions you like and tailor it for the specific development language. 

This is a wonderful architecture. However, I have noticed that this flexibility has caused a lot of inconsistencies in the user experience between developers on the same team. 
In my case we are a team of Python analysts and developers. I am frequently troubleshooting differences in user experiences - which boils down to somebody not having the right extensions.  In such a situation, we end up indentifying the missing extension and then adding it to the `.vscode\extensions.json`.

## Solution
The `extensions.json` is a great idea. I urge Microsoft to take a step forward and capture every extension that I enable , automatically added to this file. This will give transparency and explain why something is working on my workstation and not on my co-developers. Vice-versa - if I disable an extension, then immediately remove the entry from `extensions.json`.

IMHO, this will solve the burning issue of VS Code behaving differently for each developer

Thanks.

title: PendingMigrationError: navigator is now a global in nodejs thrown during module load on remote VS Code server,   causing repeated renderer crashes and Remote SSH disconnections
description:
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates -->
<!-- Please attach logs to help us diagnose your issue -->

- Copilot Chat Extension Version:0.45.0
- VS Code Version: 1.117.0
- OS Version:    
    -  Local:  macOS 15.5 (Build 24F74), Apple Silicon arm64
    - Remote: Ubuntu 20.04 (Linux 5.4.0-139-generic, x86_64)
    - Remote Node.js (bundled with VS Code server): v22.22.1
- Feature (e.g. agent/edit/ask mode):N/A — the crash occurs during module load of the bundled Copilot
    extension on the remote server, before any Copilot feature is invoked.
    Simply opening a Remote SSH window is sufficient to reproduce.
- Selected model (e.g. GPT 4.1, Claude 3.7 Sonnet):N/A — crash occurs before any model is selected or any request is made.
- Logs:
```python
PendingMigrationError: navigator is now a global in nodejs,
  please see https://aka.ms/vscode-extensions/navigator for additional info on this error.
      at get (file:///lpai/.vscode-server/bin/10c8e557c8b9f9ed0a87f61f1c9a44bde731c409/out/vs/workbench/api/node/extensionHos
  tProcess.js:831:7210)
      at .../extensions/copilot/dist/extension.js:333:63732
      at get value (.../extensions/copilot/dist/extension.js:276:5560)
      at .../extensions/copilot/dist/extension.js:358:202
      at Function.r (.../extensions/copilot/dist/extension.js:276:4544)
      at .../extensions/copilot/dist/extension.js:360:12368
      at r (.../extensions/copilot/dist/extension.js:276:4544)
      at new ZodObject (.../extensions/copilot/dist/extension.js:276:4803)
      at j0 (.../extensions/copilot/dist/extension.js:277:20590)
      at .../extensions/copilot/dist/extension.js:360:16871
      at .../extensions/copilot/dist/extension.js:1:231
      at Object.<anonymous> (.../extensions/copilot/dist/extension.js:2399:838)
      at Module._compile (node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:1705:14)
      at Object..js (node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:1838:10)
      at Module.load (node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:1441:32)
      at Function.<anonymous> (node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:1263:12)
      at i._load (.../extensionHostProcess.js:831:6589)
      at e._load (.../extensionHostProcess.js:649:28604)
      at n._load (.../extensionHostProcess.js:641:25790)
      at yP._doLoadModule (.../extensionHostProcess.js:680:1614)
```
### Description

When connecting to a remote host via Remote SSH, the version of the Copilot extension bundled inside the VS Code server package (/lpai/.vscode-server/bin/<commit>/extensions/copilot/) accesses navigator during module load — not during activation or at runtime.
 In recent versions of Node.js, navigator is now a global, which causes VS Code to throw a PendingMigrationError. Because the error is raised at module load time, it is not caught gracefully, and the remote extension host becomes unstable.

This triggers a cascade of failures every time a Remote SSH window is opened:

1. Remote extension host loads Copilot, navigator is accessed during Module._compile, PendingMigrationError is thrown
2. The remote extension host becomes unstable; VS Code surfaces the error as repeated "An unknown error occurred" notifications
3. After 3–4 such events (~2–3 minutes), the local renderer process crashes (reason: 'crashed', code: '5')
4. The Remote SSH session is immediately terminated; any open terminals and unsaved state on the remote are lost

The issue reproduces on every connection to the remote host without any user interaction.

### Observed crash sequence (from main.log)

[error] CodeWindow: renderer process gone (reason: crashed, code: 5)
[info]  Extension host with pid XXXXX exited with code: 0, signal: unknown.

This repeats every 2–3 minutes until VS Code is fully restarted or the Remote SSH window is closed.

### Key observation

The error is thrown inside Module._compile during the initial require() of copilot/dist/extension.js. This means the access to navigator is at the top level of the module (outside any function or activation callback), making it impossible for VS Code's
extension loading machinery to catch and recover from it gracefully.

### Expected behavior

Any access to navigator in the extension's Node.js code path should either be guarded with typeof navigator !== "undefined", or the top-level module code should not access browser globals unconditionally. The remote extension host should not crash as a result.

title: Copilot Autopilot (Preview) mode answers its own questions without waiting for user input
description: **Steps to Reproduce:** 1. Open Copilot Chat in VS Code and switch to **Autopilot (Preview)** mode 2. Give Copilot a task that requires a decision (e.g. "Add a way to edit groups in my UI") 3. Copilot analyzes the codebase and generates a clarification question via the `askQuestion` tool (e.g. *"Which approach do you want for editing groups? Option A or Option B?"*) 4. The modal doesn't appear at all and Copilot **immediately answers the question itself** and continues execution **Actual Result:** Copilot picks an answer on its own (e.g. *"Option A — Edit icon per card"*) and proceeds without waiting for user input. The question modal is shown but functionally useless since the agent doesn't pause. **Expected Result:** When Copilot calls `askQuestion` and displays a modal, execution should **block** until the user explicitly submits an answer. The agent should treat this as a hard pause point, not an optional hint. **Why this matters:** The `askQuestion` mechanism exists precisely for situations where the agent cannot or should not decide on its own. If the agent bypasses it, the feature is misleading, it creates the appearance of user control while ignoring the response entirely.

Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes/No

<!-- 🪓 If you answered No above, use 'Help: Start Extension Bisect' from Command Palette to try to identify the cause. -->
<!-- 📣 Issues caused by an extension need to be reported directly to the extension publisher. The 'Help > Report Issue' dialog can assist with this. -->
- VS Code Version: 1.116.0 (used in the latest code-server)
- OS Version: Browser (Chrome/Edge/Safari) running `code-server` in a Linux Container.

**Environment Note:** This issue is specific to **VS Code for the Web** (code-server). The regex is strictly applied to the incoming URI.

**Steps to Reproduce (Web Specific):**
1. Launch `code-server` or VS Code for the Web.
2. Trigger an OAuth flow that uses LocalStorageURLCallbackProvider (in my case a custom MCP server as OAuth 2.1 client).
3. Identity provider (Cognito) redirects to `https://<your-domain>/callback?code=xxx&state=yyy`.
4. Just after a successful redirect to callback url, the following error message appears in Output tab: 'Authentication failed: No authorization code received'

---

### **Technical Specifics for the Report**
In the web version, after successful redirect the callback html script writes authorization 'code' (and other parameter) to the localStorage. The **Workbench** (Main Thread) receives the 'LocalStorageURLCallback' and it fires an event with the localStorage item to the **Extension Host Process** running in backend api/node. 

The bug exists in the code that **receives** this message inside the 'Extension Host Process'. In this repo the source code is present here:
file: `/src/vs/workbench/api/common/extHostAuthentication.ts`
function: `private async waitForAuthorizationCode(expectedState: URI): Promise<{ code: string }>`
line code: `const codeMatch = /[?&]code=([^&]+)/.exec(result.query || '');`

The above code has restrictive regular expression, and if the `query` string has `code` as the first parameter then it ignores it, since it does not find leading `&` or  `?` character.

### **My temporary fix**
I was able to fix this locally in my `code-server` Docker container by patching the compiled output:
```bash
FROM codercom/code-server:latest

<!-- Describe the feature you'd like. -->

## Problem

The memory-tool stores data at a hardcoded path inside the container:
~/.vscode-server/data/User/globalStorage/github.copilot-chat/memory-tool/


In Dev Containers, this path is wiped on every container rebuild, destroying all saved memories — despite the docs saying memories "persist across sessions."

## Request

Add a setting to configure the storage path:

```json
"github.copilot.chat.memoryStoragePath": "/some/persistent/path"
```
This would allow Dev Container users to point memory storage to a bind-mounted host directory, making memories actually persistent.

title: Chat Sessions panel: allow user-defined groups or folders
description: vscode 1.117 on Mac When you work on multiple things at once, the Sessions panel becomes a wall of entries that's hard to navigate. The search doesn't really help either — it misses sessions pretty often, probably because it only matches on titles and not on the actual content of the conversations. So you end up scrolling through dozens of entries trying to find the one you need. I'd love to be able to group sessions into folders or tags, something like "Project A", "Experiments", "Done" — whatever makes sense to the user. The infrastructure already supports grouping. There's groupByDate, groupByRepository, and groupByCapped in the sessions data source. Adding a user-defined grouping mode that lets you drag sessions into named groups would follow the same pattern. ### What I'd expect: 1. Right-click a session → "Move to Group..." → pick or create a group name 2. Groups show as collapsible sections (like the existing "Today" / "Yesterday" / "More" headers) 3. The group assignment persists across restarts (stored alongside the existing archived/pinned/read state in AgentSessionsCache) 4. Sessions without a group just show at the top like they do now ### Why not just use search? Search is reactive, you already need to know what you want. Groups let you proactively organize while you work, like folders in a file explorer. The pinned feature partially solves this but it's a single bucket. With 50+ sessions from different projects, one "pinned" list isn't enough.

title: Regression in VS Code 1.117.0: Azure AI Foundry / Azure OpenAI custom models fail with HTTP 400 via Language Models -> Add Models
description:
### Environment

- VS Code: 1.117.0
- Commit: 10c8e557c8b9f9ed0a87f61f1c9a44bde731c409
- GitHub Copilot Chat: 0.44.2 (prod)
- OS: Windows 11 / win32 10.0.22621 x64

### Summary

Using an Azure AI Foundry / Azure OpenAI model added through:

`Language Models -> Add Models`

fails in VS Code 1.117.0 with an HTTP 400 error.

This worked before the recent update(s) and appears to have regressed very recently.
Not sure at which version it broke, because a few updates might have been skipped.

### Minimal configuration

The model is configured in `chatLanguageModels.json` with a custom Azure vendor entry pointing to a Responses API endpoint:

```json
[
  {
    "name": "Azure Custom Model",
    "vendor": "azure",
    "apiKey": "${input:chat.lm.secret.REDACTED}",
    "models": [
      {
        "id": "gpt-5.3-codex",
        "name": "gpt-5.3-codex",
        "url": "https://REDACTED.services.ai.azure.com/api/projects/REDACTED/openai/v1/responses",
        "toolCalling": true,
        "vision": true,
        "maxInputTokens": 128000,
        "maxOutputTokens": 16000
      }
    ]
  }
]
```

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Open VS Code 1.117.0
2. Configure or use an Azure AI Foundry / Azure OpenAI custom language model via `Language Models -> Add Models`
3. Select the model in chat
4. Send a normal prompt

### Actual Result

The request fails with:

```txt
Sorry, your request failed. Please try again.
Reason: Request Failed: 400
```

Error payload:

```json
{
  "error": {
    "message": "Invalid value: ''. Supported values are: 'apply_patch_call', 'apply_patch_call_output', 'code_interpreter_call', 'compaction', 'computer_call', 'computer_call_output', 'custom_tool_call', 'custom_tool_call_output', 'file_search_call', 'function_call', 'function_call_output', 'image_generation_call', 'item_reference', 'local_shell_call', 'local_shell_call_output', 'mcp_approval_request', 'mcp_approval_response', 'mcp_call', 'mcp_list_tools', 'message', 'reasoning', 'shell_call', 'shell_call_output', 'tool_search_call', 'tool_search_output', and 'web_search_call'.",
    "type": "invalid_request_error",
    "param": "input",
    "code": "invalid_value"
  }
}
```

Stack trace excerpt:

```txt
at Pj._provideLanguageModelResponse (...\extensions\github.copilot-chat-0.44.2\dist\extension.js:1688:13141)
at process.processTicksAndRejections (node:internal/process/task_queues:103:5)
```

### Expected Result

The Azure AI Foundry / Azure OpenAI model should answer normally, as it did before updating.

### Regression?

Yes.

This setup worked before updating to VS Code 1.117.0.

### Diagnostics

`Developer: GitHub Copilot Chat Diagnostics` shows successful connectivity to the main GitHub Copilot endpoints:

- `https://api.github.com` -> HTTP 200
- `https://api.individual.githubcopilot.com/_ping` -> HTTP 200
- `https://proxy.individual.githubcopilot.com/_ping` -> HTTP 200

Relevant user settings:

```json
"http.systemCertificatesNode": true,
"github.copilot.advanced.debug.useElectronFetcher": true,
"github.copilot.advanced.debug.useNodeFetcher": false,
"github.copilot.advanced.debug.useNodeFetchFetcher": true
```

### Direct API verification

Calling the same Azure Responses API endpoint directly outside of VS Code succeeds.

Sanitized example:

```powershell
curl.exe -X POST "https://REDACTED.services.ai.azure.com/api/projects/REDACTED/openai/v1/responses" ^
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" ^
  -H "api-key: REDACTED" ^
  -d "{\"model\":\"gpt-5.3-codex\",\"input\":[{\"type\":\"message\",\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"What is the capital of Germany?\"}]}"
```

The direct response completes successfully and returns a normal `message` output, for example:

```json
{
  "object": "response",
  "status": "completed",
  "model": "gpt-5.3-codex",
  "error": null,
  "output": [
    {
      "type": "message",
      "role": "assistant",
      "content": [
        {
          "type": "output_text",
          "text": "The capital of Germany is **Berlin**."
        }
      ],
      "status": "completed"
    }
  ]
}
```

This suggests the Azure endpoint and deployment are working, while the request generated by VS Code / GitHub Copilot Chat may be malformed.

### Notes

The error suggests that the generated Responses API payload may contain an empty or otherwise invalid `type` value somewhere inside the `input` payload.

This looks like a request formatting / serialization issue in VS Code and/or GitHub Copilot Chat when sending chat requests to Azure AI Foundry / Azure OpenAI custom models added through `Language Models -> Add Models`.

### Request

Please investigate whether VS Code 1.117.0 and/or GitHub Copilot Chat 0.44.2 is generating an invalid Responses API payload for Azure custom language models.

A direct POST to the same Responses API endpoint works successfully outside VS Code, so this seems to be specific to the VS Code / Copilot integration layer rather than the Azure deployment itself.

- VS Code Version: 1.115.0 (Universal) Commit: 41dd792b5e652393e7787322889ed5fdc58bd75b Date: 2026-04-07T22:04:57Z Electron: 39.8.5 ElectronBuildId: 13703022 Chromium: 142.0.7444.265 Node.js: 22.22.1 V8: 14.2.231.22-electron.0
- OS Version: Darwin arm64 25.3.0 (macOS)

Steps to Reproduce:
1. Configure the GitHub remote MCP server in .vscode/mcp.json:
   {
     "servers": {
       "github": {
         "type": "http",
         "url": "https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/",
         "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer ${input:github_mcp_pat}" }
       }
     }
   }

2. Open Copilot Chat in Agent mode. Confirm GitHub MCP server is
   connected and get_file_contents tool is listed and enabled.

3. Ask the agent to read any file from any GitHub repository 
   you have access to:
   "Read the file README.md from <any-org>/<any-repo>"

4. Observe the agent calls get_file_contents with correct parameters
   and receives "successfully downloaded text file (SHA: ...)" but
   has no access to actual file content. Agent retries 2-3 times
   and gives up without ever reading the file.

5. Open Output panel → GitHub Copilot Chat and observe this error:
   [error] Error from tool read_file with args
   {"filePath": "vscode-chat-response-resource://.../<filename>"}:
   File vscode-chat-response-resource://... is outside of the
   workspace, and not open in an editor, and can't be read

**Expected:** Agent receives actual file content and uses it.

**Actual:** File content silently discarded. Agent only sees
"successfully downloaded text file" and never the file content.

**Root Cause:**
The GitHub MCP server returns file content as two content blocks
per the MCP specification:
- Block 1 type:"text"     → "successfully downloaded text file"
- Block 2 type:"resource" → { uri: "repo://...", text: "<content>" }

VS Code Copilot Chat's MCP tool result parser processes only
type:"text" blocks and silently discards type:"resource" blocks.
The actual file content sits in the resource block and is never
passed to the agent.

**Proof — identical bug fixed in OpenCode (another MCP client) in
24 hours on Jan 12 2026 by updating the MCP tool result parser:**
- Issue: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/7878
- Fix merged: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/7879
- File changed: packages/opencode/src/session/prompt.ts

No server change required. Pure client-side parser update needed
in github.copilot-chat extension.

**Upstream references:**
- GitHub MCP server root cause:
  https://github.com/github/github-mcp-server/issues/607
- SDK migration that changed response format:
  https://github.blog/changelog/2025-12-10-the-github-mcp-server-adds-support-for-tool-specific-configuration-and-more/
