title: iOS codesign fails (‘resource fork… detritus not allowed’) when com.apple.provenance exists on built artifact
description:
### Steps to reproduce

Refer: github.com/flutter/flutter/issues/181103 and #180351.

Summary:
Flutter iOS simulator builds fail on macOS 26.4.1 (Tahoe) with Apple Silicon (M-series) due to a code signing error caused by extended attributes that macOS automatically adds to files but Flutter's build process does not remove.
What happens:
When running flutter run targeting an iOS simulator, the build fails during the debug_unpack_ios phase with the error:
resource fork, Finder information, or similar detritus not allowed
Command CodeSign failed with a nonzero exit code
Why it happens:
Newer versions of macOS (26/Tahoe) automatically add extended attributes to files, specifically com.apple.provenance and com.apple.fileprovider.fpfs#P:, to track file origin. Flutter's cleanup code in removeFinderExtendedAttributes (located in packages/flutter_tools/lib/src/ios/mac.dart) only removes com.apple.FinderInfo but does not remove these newer attributes. Apple's code signing tool rejects any binary that has these attributes present, causing the build to fail.
Environment:

macOS 26.4.1 (Tahoe), Apple Silicon (arm64)
Xcode installed from App Store
Flutter installed via Homebrew and also via git clone from stable branch
Issue occurs on both fresh projects and existing projects
Issue is 100% reproducible on this setup

What was tried:

flutter clean and rebuilding
Stripping attributes manually with xattr -cr
Reinstalling Flutter via Homebrew
Reinstalling Flutter via git clone from stable branch
Manually patching mac.dart to also remove com.apple.provenance and com.apple.fileprovider.fpfs#P: — patch confirmed present in file but did not resolve the issue as attributes are re-added during the Xcode build phase itself
Disabling and re-enabling System Integrity Protection (SIP)

Workaround:
None found for the iOS simulator. Running via Chrome (flutter run -d chrome) works correctly.

### Steps to reproduce



- Integrate the Flutter camera plugin:


`camera: ^0.12.0+1`

- Configure the iOS app:

> In Info.plist, allow only Portrait orientation.

- On the iOS device:

> Disable Orientation Lock from device settings.


- Launch the app and open the camera preview.

- Rotate the device between portrait and landscape modes.

### Expected results


- The camera preview should maintain correct aspect ratio and orientation.
- The preview should not appear stretched, distorted, or misaligned when the device is rotated.
- The UI should remain consistent with the allowed orientation (portrait).

### Actual results



- The camera preview becomes distorted and improperly scaled when rotating the device.
- The preview does not render correctly in either portrait or landscape mode.
- The issue occurs only when:

> Orientation lock is disabled on the device, and
> Only portrait mode is enabled in Info.plist.

Additional Observations
	•	If all orientations are enabled in Info.plist, the camera preview works correctly.
	•	If Orientation Lock is enabled on the device, the issue does not occur (regardless of orientation settings in Info.plist).
	•	The issue is specific to iOS; all scenarios work correctly on Android.

title: [Linux] Wayland Protocol Error: Buffer size must be an integer multiple of the buffer_scale
description:
<!-- 
This issue was generated with the assistance of an AI debugging agent after reproducing and diagnosing a Wayland display crash in a Flutter application (LocalSend).
-->

## Description
Flutter applications on Linux (Wayland) fail to launch and are immediately terminated by the Wayland compositor with a "Protocol error" when hi-DPI scaling (e.g., 200%) is enabled. 

This occurs because the Flutter engine requests a buffer with dimensions that are not an integer multiple of the `buffer_scale`.

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Use a Linux distribution with Wayland (e.g., Debian Trixie, GNOME 48).
2. Set display scaling to 200% (or any integer scale > 1).
3. Launch a Flutter-based Linux application natively on Wayland (e.g., LocalSend v1.17.0, compiled with Flutter 3.24.5).

### Actual Results
The application fails to start. Standard terminal output shows:
`Gdk-Message: ...: Error flushing display: Protocol error`

Running the application with `WAYLAND_DEBUG=1` reveals the exact root cause:
```text
[2170011.614] wl_display@1.error(wl_surface@36, 2, "Buffer size (452x599) must be an integer multiple of the buffer_scale (2).")
```
In this instance, a buffer height of `599` is requested with a `buffer_scale` of `2`. The Wayland compositor (Mutter) instantly terminates the client for violating the protocol requirement that buffer dimensions must be exactly divisible by the scale factor.

### Expected Results
The Flutter engine's Wayland embedder should ensure that all requested buffer dimensions are rounded or clamped to be exact integer multiples of the current `buffer_scale` before attaching the buffer to the Wayland surface.

### Environment
- **OS:** Debian GNU/Linux 13 (trixie)
- **DE:** GNOME Shell 48.7
- **Session Type:** Wayland
- **Scaling:** 200%
- **GPU:** NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090 (Driver 580.82.09)
- **Flutter Version:** 3.24.5 (Observed via LocalSend v1.17.0 release artifacts)

### Additional Context
- The issue persists regardless of distribution method (Snap, Flatpak).
- Forcing `GDK_BACKEND=x11` (XWayland) serves as a workaround, confirming the issue is isolated to the native Wayland surface rendering.
- Previous issues (e.g., #101407) reported the `Gdk-Message: Error 71 (Protocol error)` but were closed without checking the underlying `WAYLAND_DEBUG` logs to identify the buffer size violation.

title: Add FocusLifecyclePolicy to allow apps to control focus behavior during lifecycle changes
description:
### Use case

The current `FocusManager` behavior during app lifecycle transitions (foreground/background) is hardcoded per platform: on desktop and web, the primary focus is stashed and then set to the Root focus node when the app loses system foreground focus and then restored when system focus is regained, while on Android and iOS this behavior is disabled due to known issues with keyboard and autofill interactions.

There is no way for an application to override this per-platform default. This is a problem for apps that need different behavior than what the platform default provides. For example:
- **Embedded/TV platforms (e.g. RDK):** Flutter apps running on TV platforms like RDK could benefit from focus **persisting** through lifecycle transitions when switching between foreground apps. The default desktop behavior of clearing and restoring focus is often disruptive in this context and can cause unnecessary engineering complications and bugs.
- **Mobile apps** that want to opt in to focus save/restore, for whatever reason, despite it being disabled by default on Android/iOS.
- **Desktop/web apps** that want to opt out of the save/restore behavior entirely. For example, a development team I'm on uses a MacOS build of a TV app that uses d-pad navigation for quicker development. We often activate floating window mode to keep the app's window on top of all other windows. Without this feature, focusing in and out of the app's window is always jarring due to focus resetting to the root, and then back to the preserved element when the window regains focus.

### Proposal

Add a `FocusLifecyclePolicy` enum and a corresponding `FocusManager.lifecyclePolicy` property that allows apps to choose between three behaviors:
- `automatic` (default): The current platform-dependent behavior. No change for existing apps.
- `suspend`: Always save focus on background and restore on resume, regardless of platform. Enables save/restore on mobile platforms where it's currently disabled.
- `persist`: Never modify focus during lifecycle changes, regardless of platform. Focus remains on whatever node has it when the app transitions to the background.

#### Usage:
```dart
FocusManager.instance.lifecyclePolicy = FocusLifecyclePolicy.persist;
```

This is a non-breaking change — the default `automatic` policy preserves existing behavior on all platforms.

title: camera_android: race in closeCaptureSession() may cause NPE during camera shutdown
description:
### Steps to reproduce

Version
```
camera: 0.11.4
camera_android: 0.10.10+15
```

We don't have a fully deterministic repro yet, but this happens intermittently during camera shutdown/release timing windows, for example:

- app goes to background while camera is active
- camera page is popped/disposed while the camera is closing
- camera session is being recreated while another close path is already in progress

### Expected results

Closing the camera and capture session should be safe, even if multiple close/release callbacks happen very close together.

### Actual results

The app crashes with:
```
Fatal Exception: java.lang.NullPointerException
Attempt to invoke virtual method 'void android.hardware.camera2.CameraCaptureSession.close()' on a null object reference
io.flutter.plugins.camera.Camera.closeCaptureSession (Camera.java:1312)
io.flutter.plugins.camera.Camera$1.onClosed (Camera.java:409)
android.hardware.camera2.impl.CameraDeviceImpl$5.run (CameraDeviceImpl.java:198)
android.os.Handler.handleCallback (Handler.java:751)
android.os.Handler.dispatchMessage (Handler.java:95)
android.os.Looper.loop (Looper.java:154)
android.os.HandlerThread.run (HandlerThread.java:61)
```

### Code sample

Analysis
This looks like a race on the shared captureSession field in `closeCaptureSession().`

Current implementation reads the shared field more than once:

```
void closeCaptureSession() {
  if (captureSession != null) {
    Log.i(TAG, "closeCaptureSession");
    captureSession.close();
    captureSession = null;
  }
}
```

This seems vulnerable to a TOCTOU race:

callback A checks captureSession != null
another path clears captureSession
callback A dereferences captureSession again and hits NPE
A safer implementation would be:

```
void closeCaptureSession() {
  final CameraCaptureSession session = captureSession;
  captureSession = null;
  if (session == null) {
    return;
  }
  Log.i(TAG, "closeCaptureSession");
  session.close();
}
```

This avoids dereferencing a shared mutable field after another callback may already have cleared it.

title: Replace hardcoded platform identity checks in the framework with capability-based queries
description:
### Description

Currently, the Flutter framework relies on hardcoded platform identity checks (e.g., `defaultTargetPlatform` or `Theme.of(context).platform`) to determine behavior. This creates friction for out-of-tree custom embedders, who are forced to spoof their OS identity to inherit basic capabilities.

**Proposal:**
* Replace hardcoded platform identity checks within the core framework with capability-based queries (e.g., `supportsPhysicsBasedScrolling`).
* Establish and document a mechanism for custom embedders to declare their supported capabilities to the framework.
* Allow existing Flutter-maintained platforms (like Android) to serve as an extensible "base." This would allow custom platforms that share most (but not all) behaviors with a supported platform to inherit its capabilities and deviate slightly only where needed.

Here are several examples:

1. `FlexibleSpaceBar` uses `Theme.of(context).platform` to decide whether to center titles.
https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/00b14ee0eee3fc91dbf3284daff57ff1ebd22389/packages/flutter/lib/src/material/flexible_space_bar.dart#L191-L200

2. `Drawer` relies on platform checks to determine layout, semantics, and system back button presence, ex:
https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/00b14ee0eee3fc91dbf3284daff57ff1ebd22389/packages/flutter/lib/src/material/drawer.dart#L253-L259


3. `TextMagnifier` hardcodes the magnifier implementation by switching on `defaultTargetPlatform`, returning null on unrecognized platforms.
https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/00b14ee0eee3fc91dbf3284daff57ff1ebd22389/packages/flutter/lib/src/material/magnifier.dart#L47-L57

4. The `Radio.adaptive` constructor uses a switch statement to return a CupertinoRadio for Apple platforms and defaults to the standard Material radio for all others.
https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/00b14ee0eee3fc91dbf3284daff57ff1ebd22389/packages/flutter/lib/src/material/radio.dart#L518-L540

5. `Autocomplete` assigns keyboard shortcuts by switching on `defaultTargetPlatform`.
https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/00b14ee0eee3fc91dbf3284daff57ff1ebd22389/packages/flutter/lib/src/widgets/autocomplete.dart#L412-L419

title: `autosubmit` blocks merging on stale "request changes" pr
description:
## example

https://github.com/flutter/flutter/pull/184984

## reproduction steps

1) X authors PR
1) Y reviews PR with request changes
1) X makes changes
1) Y approves changes
1) X fixes merge conflicts (which invalidates all previous approvals)
1) Z approves changes

In this state the PR just has one review that is an approval, but it will fail to merge the PR with the following message:

```
autosubmit label was removed for flutter/flutter/184984, because This PR has not met approval requirements for merging. Changes were requested by {Y}, please make the needed changes and resubmit this PR.
The PR author is a member of flutter-hackers and needs 1 more review(s) in order to merge this PR.

- Merge guidelines: A PR needs at least one approved review if the author is already part of flutter-hackers or two member reviews if the author is not a member of flutter-hackers before re-applying the autosubmit label. Reviewers: If you left a comment approving, please use the "approve" review action instead.
```

## observed behavior

The PR is blocked from merging, despite the PR having only one active review which is approval.

## expected behavior

Since Y's last review was approval, and the PR has an active review from Z, it should be merged.

title: Manually Bump `dev/benchmarks/platform_views_layout` to AGP 9
description:
Instead of including this change in this massive PR: https://github.com/flutter/flutter/pull/185118,  bumping `dev/benchmarks/platform_views_layout` to AGP 9 will be done in a separate PR in case this change brings down the tree or affects a roll.

Added `dev/benchmarks/platform_views_layout` to the generate lockfiles exclusions.yaml because AGP 9 is incompatible with the current pinned `google_mobile_ads` version 5.1.0. The flutter `platform_views_layout` project can successfully build when `google_mobile_ads` is version 7.0.0, but `webview_flutter` has to be at least 4.10.0 and `webview_flutter_android` has to be at least 4.10.9.

Also, `google_mobile_ads` was manually pinned to 5.1.0 due to this xcode issue: https://github.com/flutter/flutter/issues/156912. It looks resolved, but included it just in case it isn't.

`google_mobile_ads` -> 7.0.0
`webview_flutter` -> 4.10.0

title: Proposal: Add `themeBuilder` to MaterialApp to eliminate theme duplication
description:
### Use case

Flutter recommends using `ThemeData.from(colorScheme: ...)` together with `ColorScheme.fromSeed(..., brightness: brightness)`. With this pattern, the only thing that differs between light and dark themes is `Brightness` — almost of settings not related to color (typography, shape, component themes, some of `ThemeExtension`s, etc.) are identical.

However, `MaterialApp` only accepts fully-specified `ThemeData` objects for each of `theme`, `darkTheme`, `highContrastTheme`, and `highContrastDarkTheme`. The only way to avoid duplication is to define a helper function on the user side:

```dart
MaterialApp(
  theme:              _buildTheme(Brightness.light, false),
  darkTheme:          _buildTheme(Brightness.dark,  false),
  highContrastTheme:  _buildTheme(Brightness.light, true),
  highContrastDarkTheme: _buildTheme(Brightness.dark, true),
)

ThemeData _buildTheme(Brightness brightness, bool highContrast) =>
    ThemeData.from(
      colorScheme: ColorScheme.fromSeed(
        seedColor: kSeedColor,
        brightness: brightness,
      ),
    ).copyWith(
      cardTheme: ...,
      inputDecorationTheme: ...,
      extensions: [AppColors.fromBrightness(brightness, highContrast)],
    );
```

The framework offers no first-class support for this pattern, so developers unfamiliar with it naturally write separate `ThemeData` objects for each property, leading to drift over time.

### Proposal

Add a `themeBuilder` property to `MaterialApp` with the following signature:

```dart
themeBuilder: (Brightness brightness, bool highContrast) => ThemeData
```

Example usage:

```dart
MaterialApp(
  themeBuilder: (brightness, highContrast) => ThemeData.from(
    colorScheme: ColorScheme.fromSeed(
      seedColor: Colors.blue,
      brightness: brightness,
    ),
  ).copyWith(
    cardTheme: const CardThemeData(elevation: 2),
    inputDecorationTheme: const InputDecorationTheme(
      border: OutlineInputBorder(),
    ),
    extensions: [
      AppColors.fromBrightness(
        brightness,
        highContrast,
      ),
    ],
  ),
  themeMode: ThemeMode.system,
)
```

When `themeBuilder` is provided, `MaterialApp` calls it internally with the resolved `Brightness` and `highContrast`, replacing the need for `theme`, `darkTheme`, `highContrastTheme`, and `highContrastDarkTheme`.  If dark theme is not needed, the brightness argument can simply be ignored.`themeBuilder` and those four properties would be mutually exclusive (assertion error if both are set). `themeMode` continues to work as-is.

Additionally, since there is no need to instantiate a separate `ThemeData` for each theme variant upfront, there may be a marginal performance improvement.

title: Shaders Applied Using ImageFilter.shader Do Not Use Full Child Rect When the Child Is Clipped
description:
### Steps to reproduce 1. Execute the referenced code (https://github.com/Ayodeji-Harman/flutter-imagefilter-shader-uv-issue-with-clipping) 2. Scroll through the displayed PageView, noting the behavior of the rendered "frost" shader effect (the effect can be toggled on/off in order to compare the behavior to that of the scrolling PageView page content. ### Expected results The "frost" effect should maintain the same boundaries as that of its associated page content. As the page content is scrolled, the rendered effect should be scrolled in the the same manner (position, off-screen clipping, boundaries). ### Actual results As the scrolling occurs within the PageView, the "frost" effect does not scroll in the same manner as the associated page content. The effect instead is vertically scaled such that it is displayed on-screen in its entirety. title: Dart vm-service GetStack method can deadlock by trying to lock the same MessageHandler monitor recursively
description:
### Description

With merged UI and platform threads enabled (the default on macOS), a Flutter app intermittently deadlocks permanently on startup in debug mode. The main thread freezes in the Dart VM's safepoint handler, rendering the app and the VM service completely unresponsive.

The trigger: a macOS `didChangeOcclusionState` notification fires on the main thread while the Dart VM has an active safepoint operation in progress (initiated by the VM debugger service). Because the UI and platform threads are merged, the notification handler executes `Dart_EnterIsolate` inline via `RunNowAndFlushMessages`, which blocks in `SafepointHandler::ExitSafepointLocked` waiting for the safepoint to complete. The safepoint itself is deadlocked among DartWorker threads (details below), so the main thread blocks forever.

### Steps to reproduce

This is timing-dependent and **debug-mode only** (the `kCheckForReload` OOB message path in `HandleLibMessage` is compiled out in PRODUCT builds). It reproduces in apps that:
1. Spawn multiple isolates during startup (e.g., for a database connection pool) — this creates concurrent DartWorker thread activity
2. Run in debug mode with the debugger/VM service attached (`flutter run` or IDE)
3. Use merged threads (the default on macOS since Flutter 3.33)

GC cannot trigger the same deadlock — `ConcurrentMarkTask` uses `bypass_safepoint=true`, and finalization messages bypass `PortMap::mutex_`.

In our app (SQLite wrapper with FFI, 5 isolates), the deadlock occurs roughly 1 in 5 cold launches in debug mode.

**To diagnose a deadlocked instance:** `sample <pid> 1 -mayDie` and look for `SafepointHandler` in the thread stacks.

### Root cause analysis

Thread sampling (`sample <pid> 1 -mayDie`) reveals two layers:

#### Layer 1: VM service deadlock among DartWorker threads

A VM debugger thread (Thread 40797897) requests a `kGCAndDeoptAndReload` safepoint to set a breakpoint via `Debugger::RunWithStoppedDeoptimizedWorld` (which uses `RELOAD_OPERATION_SCOPE`). This sends `kCheckForReload` OOB messages to all isolates and waits for all threads to reach safepoint level `kGCAndDeoptAndReload`. However, Thread 40797896 (handling a `GetStack` VM service request) is blocked trying to `PostMessage` and cannot reach a safepoint checkpoint. Multiple other DartWorker threads are also stuck — some processing the `kCheckForReload` message in `HandleLibMessage` → `BlockForSafepoint`, some blocked on `PortMap::mutex_` (held by Thread 40797896).

Key stacks:

```
Thread 40797897 (safepoint owner — debugger breakpoint):
  Debugger::SetBreakpointAtLineCol → RunWithStoppedDeoptimizedWorld
    → SafepointOperationScope(kGCAndDeoptAndReload) → SafepointThreads
      → WaitUntilThreadsReachedSafepointLevel ← BLOCKED

Thread 40797896 (can't reach safepoint — handling GetStack):
  Service::InvokeMethod → GetStack → MessageQueue::PrintJSON
    → Compiler::CompileFunction → NoReloadScope::~NoReloadScope
      → SendInternalLibMessage → PortMap::PostMessage (+180, holds PortMap::mutex_)
        → MessageHandler::PostMessage
          → _pthread_mutex_firstfit_lock_slow ← BLOCKED on a MessageHandler monitor

Threads 40797893/94 (blocked on safepoint):
  MessageHandler::HandleMessages → HandleMessage → HandleLibMessage
    → BlockForSafepoint → ExitSafepointLocked ← BLOCKED (Note: HandleMessages
      releases MessageHandler::monitor_ before calling HandleMessage)

Threads 40799860/61 (GC markers, blocked on PortMap::mutex_):
  ConcurrentMarkTask::Run → PortMap::PostMessage
    → _pthread_mutex_firstfit_lock_slow ← BLOCKED (PortMap::mutex_ held by 40797896)

Thread 40797645 (dart:io EventHandler, blocked on PortMap::mutex_):
  PostCObjectHelper → PortMap::PostMessage
    → _pthread_mutex_firstfit_lock_slow ← BLOCKED
```

**Notes on lock state:**
- `HandleMessages` explicitly releases `MessageHandler::monitor_` (via `ml->Exit()`) before calling `HandleMessage`, with an inline comment documenting this is intentional to avoid deadlocks. Threads 40797893/94 do NOT hold the monitor during `BlockForSafepoint`.
- Thread 40797896 holds `PortMap::mutex_` (confirmed: `PortMap::PostMessage` holds `PortMap::mutex_` via RAII `Locker` for the entire call including `handler->PostMessage()`). The `PortMap::mutex_` contention blocks the GC markers, dart:io EventHandler, and any other `PortMap::PostMessage` callers.
- Thread 40797896 is blocked on `MessageHandler::PostMessage` → `MonitorLocker ml(&monitor_)` — trying to acquire the target MessageHandler's monitor. The exact holder of this monitor could not be identified from the thread sample alone. The target appears to be Thread 40797896's own isolate's handler (via `NoReloadScope::~NoReloadScope` → `SendInternalLibMessage` to `isolate_->main_port()`), whose monitor was released by `HandleMessages` in step 5 above. This may indicate a subtlety in the `Monitor`/`pthread_mutex` interaction under high contention, or a holder not visible in the `sample` output.

#### Layer 2: Main thread pulled into the deadlock (Flutter engine)

While the VM service deadlock is in progress, a macOS `didChangeOcclusionState` notification fires on the merged UI/platform thread:

```
Main thread:
  __CFRunLoopDoBlocks → CGSDatagramReadStream::dispatchMainQueueDatagrams
    → -[FlutterAppLifecycleRegistrar handleDidChangeOcclusionState:]
      → -[FlutterEngine setApplicationState:]
        → FlutterEngineSendPlatformMessage
          → Shell::OnPlatformViewDispatchPlatformMessage
            → RunNowAndFlushMessages ← runs inline because merged threads
              → Dart_EnterIsolate → Thread::EnterIsolate → ExitSafepoint
                → SafepointHandler::ExitSafepointLocked
                  → _pthread_cond_wait ← BLOCKED FOREVER
```

The lifecycle handler calls `sendOnChannel:` synchronously from the NSNotification callback. `RunNowAndFlushMessages` detects it's on the UI thread (merged mode) and runs inline, calling `Dart_EnterIsolate`. `Dart_EnterIsolate` → `Thread::EnterIsolate` → `ExitSafepoint` blocks because the VM service safepoint is in progress and deadlocked.

There is **no reentrancy guard** in the lifecycle handler chain (`FlutterAppLifecycleRegistrar`, `FlutterEngine.setApplicationState:`, or `Shell::OnPlatformViewDispatchPlatformMessage`).

### Expected results

The app starts normally in debug mode.

### Actual results

The app deadlocks permanently. Black screen, no UI renders, no Dart code executes. The VM service is unresponsive (HTTP requests time out). Force-kill is the only recovery.

### Workaround

Disabling merged threads prevents the main thread from being pulled into the VM service deadlock:

```xml
<!-- macos/Runner/Info.plist -->
<key>FLTEnableMergedPlatformUIThread</key>
<false/>
```

Without merged threads, the VM service deadlock may still occur between DartWorker threads (debugger would hang), but the app UI remains responsive.

### Suggested fix

**Flutter engine (prevents the main thread freeze):**

The lifecycle notification handler should not synchronously call `Dart_EnterIsolate` on the merged thread. `RunNowAndFlushMessages` should use `PostTask` instead of inline execution for lifecycle messages, deferring the dispatch to the next event loop iteration:

```objc
// In FlutterEngine.mm, setApplicationState: or handleDidChangeOcclusionState:
// Option A: dispatch_async to defer out of the notification callback
dispatch_async(dispatch_get_main_queue(), ^{
    [self sendOnChannel:kFlutterLifecycleChannel message:...];
});

// Option B: modify RunNowAndFlushMessages to always PostTask for lifecycle
```

**Dart VM (fixes the underlying service deadlock):**

The lock-ordering issue between the VM debugger's safepoint request and the VM service's `PostMessage` calls needs investigation by the VM team. Thread 40797896 holds `PortMap::mutex_` and is blocked on a `MessageHandler` monitor while unable to reach a safepoint, preventing the debugger's safepoint from completing. The full thread sample is provided below for analysis.

title: Design doc: Soft hyphen (U+00AD) rendering
description:
### Document Link

https://flutter.dev/go/soft-hyphens

(Redirect PR: flutter/website#13282 — once merged the go-link will resolve; direct doc: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1w_d53wb-RMuwXmXIPq67JrZYG97XF1mDaKEoKBDt8-E)

### What problem are you solving?

Flutter text does not render a visible hyphen glyph when a line breaks on a soft hyphen (U+00AD). The line break happens, but the hyphen never appears — in contrast to every major web browser, native mobile text engine, and the Unicode specification. This makes Flutter unsuitable for any workflow relying on manual hyphenation markup (multilingual CMS content, justified/narrow-column text, long compound words in German/Dutch/Finnish, etc.).

Tracking issue: #18443 (open since 2018, 302+ reactions).

The underlying Skia fix has already landed ([CL 1208837](https://skia-review.googlesource.com/c/skia/+/1208837) at [`98daf58d`](https://github.com/google/skia/commit/98daf58d4c)) and has rolled into flutter/flutter. The behavior is gated behind `ParagraphStyle::setRenderSoftHyphens()` and Flutter needs to opt in. The design doc proposes a two-stage rollout: (1) enable globally in the engine (draft PR #185152), and (2) expose a Dart-level `hyphens` API on `ParagraphStyle`/`TextStyle` mirroring CSS `hyphens`.

title: Implement anti-aliased DrawPath for MetalSDF
description:
We should have a design doc that outlines how we are going to implement DrawPath with anti-aliasing.  Some ideas are:
1) using Inigo Quilez's SDF algorithms for paths -- It might get complicated when combing bezier with straight lines.
1) using @flar's approach of inflating meshes and burning in the alpha as vertex attribs

title: SDFs doesn't work for non-uniform rounded rects
description:
https://github.com/flutter/flutter/pull/184999 Adds support for SDF rounded rects, but it only works if the corners are uniform (ie the x and y components are the same).

`CanRenderRoundedRectWithNonUniformRadii` should be able to render with SDFs too.
label: UNKNOWN

title: profile quad+sdf vs fitted-mesh+sdf
description:
Last week we moved the geometry for UberSDF to being quads.  Since SDF rendering is behind a flag we didn't get automatic performance benchmarks on that change.  We need to run new gallery against special mesh vs quad for desktop and mobile platforms manually.

The concern is alpha overdraw and the extra fragment shader overhead when using quads versus fitted meshes.

Doing spot tests on Wonderous and our //dev/benchmarks/macrobenchmarks would be worth looking at as well.

cc @flar @walley892

title: Document how to use AI rules
description:
### Use case

We are currently working on integrating AI agents to work with project.
Ideally the presets should be as close to Flutter conventions as possible.

I saw here are rules defined to be integrated with different models:
https://github.com/flutter/flutter/tree/master/docs/rules

But it isn't documented what these files actually are representing and how they actually can be used. They are not referenced anywhere (in the flutter project).

I was also confused whether these app rules are meant for app developers or for the Flutter project itself.

### Proposal

- Explain for which purpose the rules are NOT made for (Flutter repository itself, Flutter packages (?)) or additionally I'd propose the title to be changed to `AI rules for Flutter Apps`
- Add a reference or / and explain more detailed on how to include AI rule files in a git / Flutter project (cherry on top: add an example project)
- Reference per model the first instructions or make it more clear that the limit docs also include the instructions for setup

title: Implement Vulkan Pre-rotation in Flutter Engine to eliminate Compositor overhead
description:
### Use case

In the current Flutter  Impeller Vulkan backend, the engine does not explicitly handle device orientation at the swapchain level. If the application does not perform this rotation during rendering (Pre-rotation), the Android System Compositor (SurfaceFlinger) must perform an additional transformation pass using the GPU or a hardware scaler.

Currently, even if Flutter renders a frame quickly, the system compositor still adds an avoidable "rotation tax" because the Vulkan swapchain is created with VK_SURFACE_TRANSFORM_IDENTITY_BIT_KHR instead of the surface's currentTransform.

This requires deep integration within the Flutter Engine's Vulkan swapchain management and the C++ rendering pipeline. 

### Proposal

I propose that the Flutter Engine implements Vulkan Pre-rotation as described in the Android Game Optimization guide.
https://developer.android.com/games/optimize/vulkan-prerotation

title: Text selection context menu does not reappear on non-fling scroll end
description:
## Description

When a context menu (toolbar) is visible and the user performs a short, non-fling scroll that keeps the selection in view, the toolbar does not re-appear after the scroll ends. A subsequent scroll causes the toolbar to appear at the beginning and remain visible throughout the entire scroll, overlapping UI elements like AppBars.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open an app with a scrollable TextField containing enough text to scroll (e.g., TextField(maxLines: 5, controller: TextEditingController(text: 'Hello world! ' * 200)))
2. Long press to select a word and show the context menu
3. Perform a very short, slow scroll (non-fling) — just enough to move the content slightly while keeping the selection in view
4. Release the gesture

### Expected: 
The toolbar re-appears after the scroll ends since the selection is still in view.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1e991f0c-7abd-4761-b409-48ad1ab5a667

### Actual: 
The toolbar stays hidden. A second scroll causes the toolbar to appear at the start of the scroll and remain visible throughout, never hiding.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/03b0d258-94d3-4d6a-91a2-a03b3aaa7f31

## Root cause

In _handleContextMenuOnScroll, when a ScrollEndNotification is received, a callback is registered via addPostFrameCallback to re-show the toolbar if the selection is still in view. However, addPostFrameCallback does not call scheduleFrame(). If no other mechanism independently schedules a frame, hasScheduledFrame remains false and the callback never fires.

On device without accessibility services, the only other candidate for scheduling a frame during the scroll-end transition is setIgnorePointer in ScrollPosition.beginActivity, which calls markNeedsSemanticsUpdate() on the RenderIgnorePointer. But markNeedsSemanticsUpdate() early-returns without scheduling a frame when no SemanticsOwner exists — which is the case on any device without a screen reader active:

// In RenderObject.markNeedsSemanticsUpdate():
```dart
if (!attached || owner!._semanticsOwner == null) {
  _needsSemanticsUpdate = true;
  return; // No frame scheduled
}
```

This means after a non-fling scroll (where no ballistic simulation drives further frames), no frame is ever scheduled, and the addPostFrameCallback callback sits pending indefinitely.
